sentences.zh: }}宋文帝元嘉三年五月庚午，以誅徐羨之等，讎恥已雪，幣告太廟。

translations.literal: On the gengwu day of the fifth month of the third year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen of Song, because Xu Xianzhi and others had been executed and the grievance and shame had been avenged, silk offerings were announced at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengwu day of the fifth month in the third year of Yuanjia, Emperor Wen of Song announced to the Imperial Ancestral Temple that Xu Xianzhi and his associates had been executed and the blood-debt finally avenged.

sentences.zh: 元嘉三年十二月甲寅，西征謝晦，告太廟、太社。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the third year of Yuanjia, on the day jiayin, [the emperor] marched west against Xie Hui and announced [it] to the Imperial Ancestral Temple and the Altar of Earth.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiayin day of the twelfth month in the third year of Yuanjia, the emperor marched west to campaign against Xie Hui and announced this to the Imperial Ancestral Temple and the Altar of Earth.

sentences.zh: 晦平，車駕旋軫，又告。

translations.literal: When Hui was pacified, the imperial carriage returned, and [the emperor] announced again.
translations.idiomatic: When Xie Hui was defeated, the imperial carriage returned, and the emperor made announcement once more.

sentences.zh: 元嘉六年七月，太學博士徐道娛上議曰：「伏見太廟烝嘗儀注，皇帝行事畢，出便坐，三公已上獻，太祝送神于門，然後至尊還拜，百官贊拜，乃退。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the sixth year of Yuanjia, Erudite of the Imperial Academy Xu Daoyu submitted a deliberation: "I have observed the ritual regulations for the winter and autumn sacrifices at the Imperial Ancestral Temple: when the emperor has finished performing the rites, he goes out and takes his seat; the Three Dukes and above present offerings; the Chief Invoker sends off the spirit at the gate; only then does the sovereign return to bow; the officials assist in bowing; and then they withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the sixth year of Yuanjia, Xu Daoyu, Erudite of the Imperial Academy, submitted a memorial: "I observe that in the ritual regulations for the winter and autumn sacrifices at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, once the emperor completes the rites he withdraws to his seat; the Three Dukes and above present offerings; the Chief Invoker sends off the spirit at the gate; only then does the sovereign return to bow, with the officials joining in the obeisance, before all withdraw.

sentences.zh: 謹尋清廟之道，所以肅安神也。

translations.literal: Carefully considering the way of the Clear Temple, its purpose is to reverently settle the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting on the way of the Clear Temple, its purpose is to reverently settle the spirits in their place.

sentences.zh: 禮曰，廟者貌也。

translations.literal: The Rites say: a temple is an image.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites say that a temple is an image.

sentences.zh: 神靈所馮依也。

translations.literal: It is what the spirits rely upon.
translations.idiomatic: It is what the spirits rely upon for their presence.

sentences.zh: 事亡如存，若常在也。

translations.literal: Serving the departed as if they were living— as if they were always present.
translations.idiomatic: One serves the departed as if they were still living, as though they were always present.

sentences.zh: 既不應有送神之文，自陳豆薦俎，車駕至止，並弗奉迎。

translations.literal: Since there ought not to be a text for sending off the spirit, from the presentation of beans and the offering of meat on stands, when the imperial carriage arrives and stops, none receive and welcome [the spirit].
translations.idiomatic: Since there ought to be no rite for sending off the spirit, from the presentation of offerings through the arrival of the imperial carriage, no one receives or welcomes the spirit.

sentences.zh: 夫不迎而送，送而後辭，闇短之情，實用未達。

translations.literal: Not welcoming yet sending off; sending off and only then taking leave— such dim and narrow sentiment truly fails to reach understanding.
translations.idiomatic: Not welcoming yet sending off, and only taking leave after the send-off—such confused reasoning truly fails to grasp the meaning.

sentences.zh: 按時人私祠，誠皆迎送，由於無廟，庶感降來格。

translations.literal: Considering that private sacrifices of the time indeed all welcome and send off, because they have no temple, hoping that the spirits will descend and come.
translations.idiomatic: Private sacrifices of the day do indeed include both welcome and send-off, but that is because they have no temple and hope thereby to draw the spirits down.

sentences.zh: 因心立意，非王者之禮也。

translations.literal: Following the heart to establish meaning— this is not the ritual of a true king.
translations.idiomatic: Such practices follow private sentiment rather than the ritual of a true sovereign.

sentences.zh: 儀禮雖太祝迎尸于門，此乃延尸之儀，豈是敬神之典。

translations.literal: Although the Ceremonial Rites have the Chief Invoker welcome the impersonator at the gate, this is the ceremony of receiving the impersonator— how could it be the canonical rite for revering the spirits?
translations.idiomatic: Although the Ceremonial Rites describe the Chief Invoker welcoming the impersonator at the gate, that is the ceremony of receiving the impersonator, not the canonical rite for revering the spirits.

sentences.zh: 恐於禮有疑。

translations.literal: I fear there is doubt regarding the ritual.
translations.idiomatic: I fear this raises doubts about the ritual.

sentences.zh: 謹以議上。

translations.literal: I respectfully submit this deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully submit this deliberation for consideration.

sentences.zh: 」有司奏下禮官詳判。

translations.literal: " The responsible officials memorialized that it be sent down to the ritual officers for detailed judgment.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible officials memorialized that the matter be referred to the ritual officers for detailed adjudication.

sentences.zh: 博士江邃議：「在始不迎，明在廟也。

translations.literal: Erudite Jiang Sui deliberated: "Not welcoming at the beginning shows that [the spirit] is in the temple.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Jiang Sui argued: "Not welcoming at the beginning shows that the spirit is already in the temple.

sentences.zh: 卒事而送，節孝思也。

translations.literal: Sending off when the rites are complete expresses filial thought in due measure.
translations.idiomatic: Sending off the spirit when the rites are complete expresses filial feeling in proper measure.

sentences.zh: 若不送而辭，是舍親也。

translations.literal: If one takes leave without sending off, this is abandoning one's kin.
translations.idiomatic: If one takes leave without sending off the spirit, that is abandoning one's kin.

sentences.zh: 辭而後送，是遣神也。

translations.literal: Taking leave and only then sending off is dispatching the spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Taking leave first and only then sending off the spirit amounts to dismissing the spirit.

sentences.zh: 故孝子不忍違其親，又不忍遣神。

translations.literal: Therefore the filial son cannot bear to go against his kin, nor can he bear to dispatch the spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore a filial son cannot bear to slight his kin, nor can he bear to dismiss the spirit.

sentences.zh: 是以祝史送神以成烝嘗之義。

translations.literal: Therefore the invokers and scribes send off the spirit to complete the meaning of the winter and autumn sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the invokers and scribes send off the spirit, completing the meaning of the winter and autumn sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 」博士賀道期議：「樂以迎來，哀以送往。

translations.literal: " Erudite He Daoqi deliberated: "With music one welcomes what comes; with grief one sends off what departs.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite He Daoqi argued: "Music welcomes what arrives; grief sends off what departs.

sentences.zh: 祭統『迎牲而不迎尸』。

translations.literal: The Record of Sacrifice [states]: 'Welcome the sacrificial victim but do not welcome the impersonator.'
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Sacrifice states: 'Welcome the sacrificial victim but do not welcome the impersonator.'

sentences.zh: 詩云：『鐘鼓送尸。

translations.literal: The Odes say: 'With bells and drums send off the impersonator.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes declare: 'With bells and drums one sends off the impersonator.

sentences.zh: 』鄭云：『尸，神象也。

translations.literal: ' Zheng [Xuan] says: 'The impersonator is the image of the spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan says: 'The impersonator is the image of the spirit.

sentences.zh: 』與今儀注不迎而後送，若合符契。

translations.literal: ' This accords with the present ritual regulations of not welcoming but then sending off, as if matching seal and tally.
translations.idiomatic: This accords with the present ritual regulations of not welcoming but then sending off, as if matching seal and tally.

sentences.zh: 」博士荀萬秋議：「古之事尸，與今之事神，其義一也。

translations.literal: " Erudite Xun Wanqiu deliberated: "Serving the impersonator in antiquity and serving the spirit today share the same meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Xun Wanqiu argued: "Serving the impersonator in antiquity and serving the spirit today share the same meaning.

sentences.zh: 周禮，尸出，送于廟門，拜，尸不顧。

translations.literal: In the Rites of Zhou, when the impersonator goes out, [one] sends [him] off at the temple gate, bows, and the impersonator does not look back.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou states that when the impersonator departs, he is sent off at the temple gate with a bow, and the impersonator does not look back.

sentences.zh: 詩云：『鐘鼓送尸。

translations.literal: The Odes say: 'With bells and drums send off the impersonator.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes declare: 'With bells and drums one sends off the impersonator.

sentences.zh: 』則送神之義，其來久矣。

translations.literal: ' Thus the meaning of sending off the spirit has long existed.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the meaning of sending off the spirit has existed since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 記曰：『迎牲而不迎尸，別嫌也。

translations.literal: The Record says: 'Welcome the sacrificial victim but do not welcome the impersonator— this distinguishes suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: The Record says: 'Welcome the sacrificial victim but do not welcome the impersonator—this distinguishes what might arouse suspicion.

sentences.zh: 尸在門外，則疑於臣；

translations.literal: When the impersonator is outside the gate, he is suspected as a minister;
translations.idiomatic: When the impersonator is outside the gate, he appears like a minister;

sentences.zh: 入廟中，則全於君。

translations.literal: entering the temple, he is complete as a lord.
translations.idiomatic: once inside the temple, he is fully treated as a lord.

sentences.zh: 君在門外，則疑於君，入廟，則全於臣。

translations.literal: When the lord is outside the gate, he is suspected as a lord; entering the temple, he is complete as a minister.
translations.idiomatic: When the lord is outside the gate, he appears like a lord; once inside the temple, he is fully treated as a minister.

sentences.zh: 是故不出者，明君臣之義。

translations.literal: Therefore not going out clarifies the meaning of lord and minister.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore not going out to welcome clarifies the distinction between lord and minister.

sentences.zh: 』」邃等三人謂舊儀為是，唯博士陳珉同道娛議。

translations.literal: '" Jiang Sui and the other three held the old ritual to be correct; only Erudite Chen Min agreed with Xu Daoyu's deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Sui and the other three held the old ritual to be correct; only Erudite Chen Min agreed with Xu Daoyu's view.

sentences.zh: 參詳「邃等議雖未盡，然皆依擬經禮。

translations.literal: Upon detailed comparison: "Although the deliberations of Jiang Sui and the others are not exhaustive, they all follow and model the canonical rites.
translations.idiomatic: Upon detailed review: "Although the deliberations of Jiang Sui and the others are not exhaustive, they all follow the canonical rites.

sentences.zh: 道娛、珉所據難從。

translations.literal: What Daoyu and Min rely upon is hard to follow.
translations.idiomatic: The grounds cited by Daoyu and Min are difficult to accept.

sentences.zh: 今眾議不一，宜遵舊體」。

translations.literal: Now the collective deliberations are not unified; the old form should be followed."
translations.idiomatic: Since the deliberations are divided, the old form should be followed."

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉六年九月，太學博士徐道娛上議曰：「祠部下十月三日殷祠，十二日烝祀。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the sixth year of Yuanjia, Erudite of the Imperial Academy Xu Daoyu submitted a deliberation: "The Department of Sacrifices schedules the yin sacrifice on the third day of the tenth month and the winter sacrifice on the twelfth day.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the sixth year of Yuanjia, Xu Daoyu, Erudite of the Imperial Academy, submitted a memorial: "The Department of Sacrifices schedules the yin sacrifice on the third day of the tenth month and the winter sacrifice on the twelfth day.

sentences.zh: 謹按禘祫之禮，三年一，五年再。

translations.literal: Carefully considering the ritual of di and he: once in three years, twice in five years.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting on the ritual of di and he sacrifices: once every three years, twice every five years.

sentences.zh: 公羊所謂五年再殷祭也。

translations.literal: This is what the Gongyang [Commentary] calls twice performing the yin sacrifice in five years.
translations.idiomatic: This is what the Gongyang Commentary calls performing the yin sacrifice twice in five years.

sentences.zh: 在四時之間，周禮所謂凡四時之間祀也。

translations.literal: Between the four seasons— what the Rites of Zhou call sacrifices between all four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Held between the four seasons—what the Rites of Zhou calls sacrifices between all four seasons.

sentences.zh: 蓋歷歲節月無定，天子諸侯，先後弗同。

translations.literal: Generally, as years and seasonal months are not fixed, emperors and feudal lords differ in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: Since the months of the calendar year were not fixed, emperors and feudal lords differed in the sequence of their sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 禮稱『天子祫嘗，諸侯烝祫。

translations.literal: The Rites say: 'The Son of Heaven performs he and chang; feudal lords perform winter and he.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites state: 'The Son of Heaven performs the he and chang sacrifices; feudal lords perform the winter and he sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 有田則祭，無田則薦』。

translations.literal: When there are fields, then sacrifice; when there are no fields, then present [offerings].'
translations.idiomatic: When there are fields, then sacrifice; when there are no fields, then present offerings.'

sentences.zh: 鄭注：『天子先祫然後時祭，諸侯先時祭然後祫。

translations.literal: Zheng's annotation: 'The Son of Heaven first performs he and then the seasonal sacrifices; feudal lords first perform the seasonal sacrifices and then he.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan annotates: 'The Son of Heaven first performs he and then the seasonal sacrifices; feudal lords first perform the seasonal sacrifices and then he.

sentences.zh: 有田者既祭又薦新。

translations.literal: Those with fields both sacrifice and present new [offerings].
translations.idiomatic: Those with fields both sacrifice and present new harvest offerings.

sentences.zh: 祭以首時，薦以仲月。

translations.literal: Sacrifice at the first season; present [offerings] in the middle month.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice at the first season; present offerings in the middle month.

sentences.zh: 』然則大祭四祀，其月各異。

translations.literal: ' Thus the great sacrifices of the four seasonal rites each fall in different months.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the four great seasonal sacrifices each fall in different months.

sentences.zh: 天子以孟月殷，仲月烝，諸侯孟月嘗，仲月祫也。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven performs yin in the first month [of the season], winter in the second month; feudal lords perform chang in the first month, he in the second month.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven performs yin in the first month of the season and winter in the second; feudal lords perform chang in the first month and he in the second.

sentences.zh: 春秋僖公八年秋七月，禘。

translations.literal: In the Spring and Autumn Annals, in the eighth year of Duke Xi, in the seventh month of autumn, di.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals records that in the seventh month of autumn in the eighth year of Duke Xi, a di sacrifice was held.

sentences.zh: 文公二年八月，大事于太廟。

translations.literal: In the second year of Duke Wen, in the eighth month, a great affair at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the second year of Duke Wen, a great sacrifice was held at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 穀梁傳曰：『著祫嘗也。

translations.literal: The Guliang Commentary says: 'Making clear he and chang.
translations.idiomatic: The Guliang Commentary says: 'This records he and chang.

sentences.zh: 』昭公十五年二月，『有事于武宮』。

translations.literal: ' In the fifteenth year of Duke Zhao, in the second month, 'there was an affair at the Martial Temple.'
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fifteenth year of Duke Zhao, 'there was an affair at the Martial Temple.'

sentences.zh: 左傳曰：『禮也。

translations.literal: The Zuo Commentary says: 'It accorded with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Commentary says: 'This accorded with ritual.

sentences.zh: 』又周禮『仲冬享烝』。

translations.literal: ' Further, the Rites of Zhou [state]: 'In mid-winter, perform the winter offering.'
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou also states: 'In mid-winter, perform the winter offering.'

sentences.zh: 月令『季秋嘗稻』。

translations.literal: The Monthly Ordinances [state]: 'In the last month of autumn, present the new rice.'
translations.idiomatic: The Monthly Ordinances state: 'In the last month of autumn, present the new rice.'

sentences.zh: 晉春烝曲沃，齊十月嘗太公，此並孟仲區別不共之明文矣。

translations.literal: Jin performed the winter sacrifice at Quwo in spring; Qi presented chang to Lord Tai in the tenth month— these all clearly distinguish first and second months as not shared.
translations.idiomatic: Jin held the winter sacrifice at Quwo in spring; Qi presented chang to Lord Tai in the tenth month—these are all explicit texts distinguishing the first and second months as separate occasions.

sentences.zh: 凡祭必先卜，日用丁巳，如不從，進卜遠日。

translations.literal: All sacrifices must first be divined; the day uses ding and si; if not followed, advance to divining a more distant day.
translations.idiomatic: All sacrifices must first be divined, preferring days ding and si; if these are unfavorable, one advances to divining a more distant day.

sentences.zh: 卜未吉，豈容二事，推期而往，理尤可知。

translations.literal: If divination is not auspicious, how could two affairs be accommodated? Postponing the date and proceeding— the principle is especially clear.
translations.idiomatic: If divination is not auspicious, how could two sacrifices be accommodated? Postponing the date is clearly the proper course.

sentences.zh: 尋殷烝祀重，祭薦禮輕。

translations.literal: Considering that the yin and winter sacrifices are heavy, while the sacrificial presentation rites are light.
translations.idiomatic: The yin and winter sacrifices are weighty rites, while sacrificial presentation is lighter.

sentences.zh: 輕尚異月，重寧反同。

translations.literal: The light still differs in month— how could the heavy instead be the same?
translations.idiomatic: If even the lighter rites fall in different months, how could the weightier ones be held in the same month?

sentences.zh: 且『祭不欲數，數則瀆』。

translations.literal: Moreover, 'One does not wish sacrifices to be frequent; if frequent, then profane.'
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, 'Sacrifices should not be frequent; if frequent, they become profane.'

sentences.zh: 今隔旬頻享，恐於禮為煩。

translations.literal: Now, enjoying offerings every ten days apart— I fear this is burdensome to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Holding offerings only ten days apart may be excessively burdensome in ritual terms.

sentences.zh: 自經緯墳誥，都無一月兩獻，先儒舊說，皆云殊朔。

translations.literal: From the classics, weft texts, and tomb edicts, there is none with two presentations in one month; the old explanations of former scholars all say different new moons.
translations.idiomatic: From the classics, commentaries, and tomb edicts, none records two presentations in one month; former scholars all say they fall on different new moons.

sentences.zh: 晉代相承，未審其原。

translations.literal: The Jin dynasty handed this down in succession; the origin has not been examined.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin dynasty handed this practice down, but its origin has not been examined.

sentences.zh: 國事之重，莫大乎祀。

translations.literal: Among the weighty affairs of state, none is greater than sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Of the weighty affairs of state, none surpasses sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 愚管膚淺，竊以惟疑。

translations.literal: My shallow and meager understanding privately harbors doubt.
translations.idiomatic: My shallow understanding privately harbors doubt.

sentences.zh: 請詳告下議。

translations.literal: I request detailed report and referral for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: I request that this be reported in detail and referred for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 」寢不報。

translations.literal: " [The memorial] was shelved without response.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was shelved without response.

sentences.zh: 元嘉七年四月乙丑，有司奏曰：「禮喪服傳云：『有死於宮中者，則為之三月不舉祭。

translations.literal: On the yichou day of the fourth month of the seventh year of Yuanjia, the responsible officials memorialized: "The Record of Mourning Garments in the Rites says: 'When someone dies in the palace, then for this [one] does not perform sacrifices for three months.
translations.idiomatic: On the yichou day of the fourth month in the seventh year of Yuanjia, the responsible officials memorialized: "The Record of Mourning Garments in the Rites states: 'When someone dies in the palace, sacrifices are suspended for three months.

sentences.zh: 』今礿祀既戒，而掖庭有故。

translations.literal: ' Now the yue sacrifice has already been announced, yet there is an incident in the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: The yue sacrifice has already been announced, yet there has been a death in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 下太常依禮詳正。

translations.literal: Refer to the Minister of Ceremonies to examine and correct according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Refer the matter to the Minister of Ceremonies for detailed adjudication according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 太學博士江邃、袁朗、徐道娛、陳珉等議，參互不同。

translations.literal: Erudites of the Imperial Academy Jiang Sui, Yuan Lang, Xu Daoyu, Chen Min, and others deliberated, their views crossing and differing.
translations.idiomatic: Erudites Jiang Sui, Yuan Lang, Xu Daoyu, Chen Min, and others deliberated, but their views differed.

sentences.zh: 殿中曹郎中領祠部謝元議以為：『遵依禮傳，使有司行事，於義為安。

translations.literal: Langzhong of the Palace Secretariat Cao Bureau, head of the Sacrifices Section, Xie Yuan, deliberated that: 'Following the ritual records and having the responsible officials perform the rites accords with propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Yuan, Langzhong of the Palace Secretariat's Cao Bureau and head of the Sacrifices Section, argued that following the ritual records and having the responsible officials perform the rites would be proper.

sentences.zh: 』輒重參詳。

translations.literal: ' [The matter] was again referred for detailed comparison.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was again referred for detailed review.

sentences.zh: 宗廟敬重，饗祀精明。

translations.literal: The ancestral temple is reverently weighty; feasting sacrifices must be clear and bright.
translations.idiomatic: The ancestral temple demands the utmost reverence; feasting sacrifices must be performed with clarity and precision.

sentences.zh: 雖聖情罔極，必在親奉。

translations.literal: Although the sage's feeling knows no limit, [the rite] must be personally performed.
translations.idiomatic: Although the sovereign's devotion knows no limit, he should ideally perform the rite in person.

sentences.zh: 然苟曰有疑，則情以禮屈。

translations.literal: Yet if there is said to be doubt, then feeling yields to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when doubt arises, personal feeling must yield to ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 無所稱述，於義有據。

translations.literal: Without anything to declare, in propriety there is basis.
translations.idiomatic: Without requiring the sovereign to declare anything, this course has proper grounds.

sentences.zh: 請聽如元所上。

translations.literal: I request approval as Yuan submitted.
translations.idiomatic: I request approval of Yuan's proposal.

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: " The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十年十二月癸酉，太祝令徐閏刺署：「典宗廟社稷祠祀薦五牲，牛羊豕雞並用雄。

translations.literal: On the guiyou day of the twelfth month of the tenth year of Yuanjia, Director of Invokers Xu Run submitted a memorial: "In managing sacrifices at the Imperial Ancestral Temple and the Altar of Earth and Grain, when presenting the five sacrificial animals, ox, sheep, pig, and chicken are all to use males.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiyou day of the twelfth month in the tenth year of Yuanjia, Xu Run, Director of Invokers, submitted a memorial: "In managing sacrifices at the Imperial Ancestral Temple and the Altar of Earth and Grain, the five sacrificial animals—ox, sheep, pig, and chicken—are all to be male.

sentences.zh: 其一種市買，由來送雌。

translations.literal: One kind purchased at market has from the beginning been sent as female.
translations.idiomatic: One kind, purchased at market, has always been supplied as female.

sentences.zh: 竊聞周景王時，賓起見雄雞自斷其尾，曰：『雞憚犧，不祥。

translations.literal: I have heard that in the time of King Jing of Zhou, Bin Qi saw a male chicken break off its own tail and said: 'The chicken fears being a sacrificial victim— inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that in the time of King Jing of Zhou, Bin Qi saw a rooster break off its own tail and said: 'The rooster fears becoming a sacrificial victim—this is inauspicious.

sentences.zh: 』今何以用雌，求下禮官詳正。

translations.literal: ' Why now use females? I request referral to the ritual officers for detailed correction.
translations.idiomatic: Why then are females used now? I request referral to the ritual officers for detailed adjudication.

sentences.zh: 」勒太學依禮詳據。

translations.literal: " [An order] commanded the Imperial Academy to examine and cite according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: An order commanded the Imperial Academy to examine the matter and cite ritual authority.

sentences.zh: 博士徐道娛等議稱：「案禮孟春之月，『是月也，犧牲無用牝』。

translations.literal: Erudite Xu Daoyu and others deliberated, stating: "Considering the Rites, in the month of early spring: 'In this month, sacrificial victims do not use females.'
translations.idiomatic: Xu Daoyu and other erudites argued: "The Rites state that in the month of early spring, 'In this month, sacrificial victims do not use females.'

sentences.zh: 如此，是春月不用雌爾，秋冬無禁。

translations.literal: Thus, it is only in spring months that females are not used; in autumn and winter there is no prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: Thus females are prohibited only in spring; autumn and winter impose no such restriction.

sentences.zh: 雄雞斷尾，自可是春月。

translations.literal: The male chicken breaking off its tail could naturally have been a spring month.
translations.idiomatic: The rooster breaking off its tail could naturally have occurred in a spring month.

sentences.zh: 」太常丞司馬操議：「尋月令孟春『命祀山林川澤，犧牲無用牝』。

translations.literal: " Vice Director of Ceremonies Sima Cao deliberated: "Considering the Monthly Ordinances for early spring: 'Order sacrifice to mountains, forests, rivers, and marshes; sacrificial victims do not use females.'
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Sima Cao argued: "The Monthly Ordinances for early spring state: 'Order sacrifice to mountains, forests, rivers, and marshes; sacrificial victims do not use females.'

sentences.zh: 若如學議，春祠三牲以下，便應一時俱改，以從月令，何以偏在一雞。

translations.literal: If as the academy deliberation [holds], then for spring sacrifices the three sacrificial animals and below should all be changed at once to follow the Monthly Ordinances— why single out only the chicken?
translations.idiomatic: If the academy's view is accepted, then for spring sacrifices the three sacrificial animals and below should all be changed at once to follow the Monthly Ordinances—why single out only the chicken?

sentences.zh: 」重更勒太學議答。

translations.literal: " [An order] again commanded the Imperial Academy to deliberate and respond.
translations.idiomatic: An order again commanded the Imperial Academy to deliberate and respond.

sentences.zh: 博士徐道娛等又議稱：「凡宗祀牲牝不一，前惟月令不用牝者，蓋明在春必雄，秋冬可雌，非以山林同宗廟也。

translations.literal: Erudite Xu Daoyu and others again deliberated, stating: "Generally, sacrificial animals for ancestral rites differ in male and female; previously only the Monthly Ordinances' prohibition on females shows clearly that in spring they must be male, while in autumn and winter females may be used— not that mountain forests and the ancestral temple are the same.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Daoyu and other erudites argued again: "Sacrificial animals for ancestral rites differ in sex; the Monthly Ordinances' prohibition on females shows only that in spring they must be male, while in autumn and winter females may be used—not that sacrifices to mountains and forests are identical to ancestral temple rites.

sentences.zh: 四牲不改，在雞偏異，相承來久，義或有由，誠非末學所能詳究。

translations.literal: The four animals are not changed; only the chicken is singled out as different— handed down for long, the reason may exist; truly this is not something a lesser scholar can exhaustively investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The four other animals remain unchanged while only the chicken is treated differently—a practice long handed down whose rationale may exist, but which a lesser scholar cannot fully investigate.

sentences.zh: 求詳議告報，如所稱令。

translations.literal: I request detailed deliberation and report, as the director stated.
translations.idiomatic: I request detailed deliberation and report, as the director proposed.

sentences.zh: 」參詳閏所稱粗有證據，宜如所上。

translations.literal: " Upon detailed comparison, what Run stated has rough evidence; [the proposal] should be as submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Upon detailed review, Run's proposal has reasonable evidence and should be approved as submitted.

sentences.zh: 自今改用雄雞。

translations.literal: From now on, male chickens are to be used.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth male chickens are to be used.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝孝建三年五月丁巳，詔以第四皇子出紹江夏王太子叡為後。

translations.literal: On the dingsi day of the fifth month of the third year of Xiaojian under Emperor Xiaowu, an edict ordered the fourth prince to go out and succeed Prince Rui of Jiangxia as heir.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingsi day of the fifth month in the third year of Xiaojian, Emperor Xiaowu issued an edict ordering the fourth prince to leave his own line and succeed Prince Rui of Jiangxia as heir.

sentences.zh: 有司奏：「皇子出後，檢未有告廟先例，輒勒二學禮官議正，應告與不？

translations.literal: The responsible officials memorialized: "When a prince goes out to become an heir, examination finds no precedent for announcing to the temple. [We] urgently command the two academies' ritual officers to deliberate and correct whether announcement should be made or not.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible officials memorialized: "When a prince leaves his line to become an heir elsewhere, no precedent for announcing to the temple has been found. We urgently command the ritual officers of both academies to determine whether such an announcement should be made.

sentences.zh: 告者為告幾室？

translations.literal: If announced, to how many chambers should announcement be made?
translations.idiomatic: If an announcement is made, to how many chambers should it be directed?

sentences.zh: 」太學博士傅休議：「禮無皇子出後告廟明文。

translations.literal: " Erudite Fu Xiu of the Imperial Academy deliberated: "The Rites contain no explicit text on announcing to the temple when a prince goes out to become an heir.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Fu Xiu argued: "The Rites contain no explicit text on announcing to the temple when a prince goes out to become an heir.

sentences.zh: 晉太康四年，封北海王寔紹廣漢殤王後，告于太廟。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taikang under Jin, when Prince Shi of Beihai was enfeoffed to succeed the posthumous Prince of Guanghan, announcement was made at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taikang under Jin, Prince Shi of Beihai was enfeoffed to succeed the posthumous Prince of Guanghan, and the court announced this at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 漢初帝各異廟，故告不必同。

translations.literal: In early Han each emperor had a separate temple, so announcements need not be identical.
translations.idiomatic: In early Han each emperor had a separate temple, so announcements need not be made to all alike.

sentences.zh: 自漢明帝以來，乃共堂各室，魏、晉依之。

translations.literal: From Emperor Ming of Han onward, they shared one hall with separate chambers; Wei and Jin followed this.
translations.idiomatic: From Emperor Ming of Han onward, emperors shared one hall with separate chambers; Wei and Jin followed this practice.

sentences.zh: 今既共堂，若獨告一室，而闕諸室，則於情未安。

translations.literal: Now that they share one hall, if announcement is made to only one chamber while omitting the others, sentiment would not be at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Now that they share one hall, announcing to only one chamber while omitting the others would be emotionally unsatisfactory.

sentences.zh: 」太常丞庾亮之議：「案禮『大事則告祖禰，小事則特告禰』。

translations.literal: " Vice Director of Ceremonies Yu Liangzhi deliberated: "Considering the Rites: 'For great affairs, announce to the ancestral and immediate forebears; for small affairs, announce specially to the immediate forebear.'
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Yu Liangzhi argued: "The Rites state: 'For great affairs, announce to the ancestral and immediate forebears; for small affairs, announce specially to the immediate forebear.'

sentences.zh: 今皇子出嗣，宜告禰廟。

translations.literal: Now that the prince goes out to succeed another line, announcement should be made at the immediate forebear's chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Since the prince is leaving to succeed another line, announcement should be made at the immediate forebear's chamber.

sentences.zh: 」祠部朱膺之議以為：「有事告廟，蓋國之常典。

translations.literal: " Sacrifices Section Zhu Yingzhi deliberated that: "Making announcement to the temple when there is an affair is a regular state ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yingzhi of the Sacrifices Section argued: "Announcing affairs to the temple is a regular state ceremony.

sentences.zh: 今皇子出紹，事非常均。

translations.literal: Now the prince goes out to succeed another line— the affair is by no means ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: The prince's departure to succeed another line is by no means an ordinary affair.

sentences.zh: 愚以為宜告。

translations.literal: In my humble view, announcement should be made.
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view, an announcement should be made.

sentences.zh: 賀循云，古禮異廟，唯謁一室是也。

translations.literal: He Xun said that in ancient ritual with separate temples, visiting only one chamber was correct.
translations.idiomatic: He Xun held that in ancient ritual, when temples were separate, visiting only one chamber was the proper practice.

sentences.zh: 既皆共廟，而闕於諸帝，於情未安。

translations.literal: Since all now share one temple, yet the other emperors are omitted, sentiment would not be at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Since all now share one temple, omitting the other emperors would be emotionally unsatisfactory.

sentences.zh: 謂循言為允，宜在皆告。

translations.literal: I hold Xun's statement to be acceptable; announcement should be made to all.
translations.idiomatic: I hold Xun's view to be acceptable; announcement should be made to all chambers.

sentences.zh: 」兼右丞殿中郎徐爰議以為：「國之大事，必告祖禰。

translations.literal: " Concurrent Right Director and Palace Attendant Xu Ai deliberated that: "The great affairs of state must be announced to the ancestral and immediate forebears.
translations.idiomatic: Concurrent Right Director and Palace Attendant Xu Ai argued: "The great affairs of state must be announced to the ancestral and immediate forebears.

sentences.zh: 皇子出嗣，不得謂小。

translations.literal: A prince going out to succeed another line cannot be called a small affair.
translations.idiomatic: A prince leaving to succeed another line cannot be considered a minor affair.

sentences.zh: 昔第五皇子承統廬陵，備告七廟。

translations.literal: In former times when the fifth prince succeeded to Luling, announcement was made at all seven temples.
translations.idiomatic: When the fifth prince formerly succeeded to Luling, announcement was made at all seven temples.

sentences.zh: 」參議以爰議為允。

translations.literal: " Upon comparison, Xu's deliberation was held acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Upon review, Xu's deliberation was held acceptable.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 大明元年六月己卯朔，詔以前太子步兵校尉祗男歆紹南豐王朗。

translations.literal: On the first day jimao of the sixth month of the first year of Daming, an edict ordered that Xin, son of the former Director of Footsoldiers of the Heir Apparent Zhi, succeed Prince Lang of Nanfeng.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day jimao of the sixth month in the first year of Daming, an edict ordered that Xin, son of the former Director of Footsoldiers of the Heir Apparent Zhi, succeed Prince Lang of Nanfeng.

sentences.zh: 有司奏：「朗先嗣營陽，告廟臨軒。

translations.literal: The responsible officials memorialized: "Lang formerly succeeded to Yingyang; announcement was made at the temple before the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible officials memorialized: "Lang formerly succeeded to Yingyang, with announcement made at the temple before the imperial throne.

sentences.zh: 檢繼體為舊，不告廟臨軒。

translations.literal: Examination shows that continuing the line is old practice, without announcement at the temple before the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Examination shows that continuing an existing line is established practice and does not require announcement at the temple before the throne.

sentences.zh: 」下禮官議正。

translations.literal: " Refer to the ritual officers for deliberation and correction.
translations.idiomatic: Refer the matter to the ritual officers for adjudication.

sentences.zh: 太學博士王燮之議：「南豐昔別開土宇，以紹營陽，義同始封，故有臨軒告廟之禮。

translations.literal: Erudite Wang Xiezhi of the Imperial Academy deliberated: "Nanfeng formerly opened separate territory to succeed Yingyang; the meaning is the same as initial enfeoffment, hence there was the ritual of announcing at the temple before the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Wang Xiezhi argued: "Nanfeng formerly received separate territory to succeed Yingyang; the meaning was the same as initial enfeoffment, hence the ritual of announcing at the temple before the throne.

sentences.zh: 今歆奉詔出嗣，則成繼體，先爵猶存，事是傳襲，不應告廟臨軒。

translations.literal: Now Xin, receiving the edict to go out and succeed, then completes the continuation of the line; the former title still exists; the affair is one of transmission and inheritance— announcement at the temple before the throne should not be made.
translations.idiomatic: Now Xin, receiving the edict to go out and succeed, completes the continuation of an existing line; the former title still stands; this is a matter of transmission and inheritance—announcement at the temple before the throne should not be required.

sentences.zh: 」祠部郎朱膺之議：「南豐王嗣爵封已絕，聖恩垂矜，特詔繼茅土，復申義同始封，為之告廟臨軒。

translations.literal: " Langzhong of the Sacrifices Section Zhu Yingzhi deliberated: "The succession and enfeoffment of the Prince of Nanfeng had already ceased; by sagely favor he was specially enfeoffed by edict to continue the fief; again the meaning is the same as initial enfeoffment— announcement at the temple before the throne was made for him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yingzhi, Langzhong of the Sacrifices Section, argued: "The Prince of Nanfeng's succession and enfeoffment had already ceased; by imperial favor he was specially re-enfeoffed by edict to continue the fief; again the meaning was the same as initial enfeoffment—announcement at the temple before the throne was made for him.

sentences.zh: 」殿中郎徐爰議：「營陽繼體皇基，身亡封絕，恩詔追封，錫以一城。

translations.literal: " Palace Attendant Xu Ai deliberated: "Yingyang continued the imperial foundation; when he died the enfeoffment ceased; by favoring edict he was posthumously enfeoffed and granted one city.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Xu Ai argued: "Yingyang continued the imperial foundation; when he died the enfeoffment ceased; by a favoring edict he was posthumously enfeoffed and granted one city.

sentences.zh: 既始啟建茅土，故宜臨軒告廟。

translations.literal: Since he first opened and established the fief, announcement at the temple before the throne was appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Since he had first opened and established the fief, it was fitting to announce this at the temple before the throne.

sentences.zh: 今歆繼後南豐，彼此俱為列國，長沙、南豐，自應各告其祖，豈關太廟。

translations.literal: Now Xin succeeds Nanfeng; both are equally feudal states; Changsha and Nanfeng should each announce to their own ancestors— how could this concern the Imperial Ancestral Temple?
translations.idiomatic: Now Xin succeeds Nanfeng; both are equally feudal states; Changsha and Nanfeng should each announce to their own ancestors—how could this concern the Imperial Ancestral Temple?

sentences.zh: 事非始封，不合臨軒。

translations.literal: The affair is not initial enfeoffment; it does not accord with announcement before the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The affair is not initial enfeoffment and does not warrant announcement before the throne.

sentences.zh: 同博士王燮之議。

translations.literal: [This is] the same as Erudite Wang Xiezhi's deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: This accords with Erudite Wang Xiezhi's view.

sentences.zh: 」參詳，爰議為允。

translations.literal: " Upon detailed comparison, Xu's deliberation was held acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Upon detailed review, Xu's deliberation was held acceptable.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 大明三年六月乙丑，有司奏：「來七月十五日，嘗祠太廟、章皇太后廟，輿駕親奉。

translations.literal: On the yichou day of the sixth month of the third year of Daming, the responsible officials memorialized: "On the fifteenth day of the coming seventh month, chang sacrifice will be offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple and the temple of Empress Dowager Zhang; the imperial carriage will personally attend.
translations.idiomatic: On the yichou day of the sixth month in the third year of Daming, the responsible officials memorialized: "On the fifteenth day of the coming seventh month, chang sacrifice will be offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple and the temple of Empress Dowager Zhang, with the imperial carriage in personal attendance.

sentences.zh: 而乘輿辭廟親戎，太子合親祠與不？

translations.literal: Yet the imperial carriage will take leave of the temple for personal military affairs— should the Heir Apparent personally perform the sacrifice or not?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the imperial carriage will take leave of the temple for personal military affairs—should the Heir Apparent personally perform the sacrifice or not?

sentences.zh: 且今月二十四日，第八皇女夭。

translations.literal: Moreover, on the twenty-fourth day of this month, the eighth imperial daughter died young.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, on the twenty-fourth day of this month, the eighth imperial daughter died in infancy.

sentences.zh: 案禮『宮中有故，三月不舉祭』。

translations.literal: Considering the Rites: 'When there is an incident in the palace, do not perform sacrifices for three months.'
translations.idiomatic: The Rites state: 'When there is an incident in the palace, sacrifices are suspended for three months.'

sentences.zh: 皇太子入住上宮，於事有疑。

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent resides in the Upper Palace; in the affair there is doubt.
translations.idiomatic: The Heir Apparent resides in the Upper Palace, which raises doubts about the matter.

sentences.zh: 」下禮官議正。

translations.literal: " Refer to the ritual officers for deliberation and correction.
translations.idiomatic: Refer the matter to the ritual officers for adjudication.

sentences.zh: 太學博士司馬興之議：「竊惟『國之大事，在祀與戎』。

translations.literal: Erudite Sima Xingzhi of the Imperial Academy deliberated: "I respectfully consider that 'the great affairs of a state lie in sacrifice and war.'
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Sima Xingzhi argued: "I respectfully note that 'the great affairs of a state lie in sacrifice and war.'

sentences.zh: 皇太子有撫軍之道，而無專御之義，戎既如之，祀亦宜然。

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent has the way of pacifying the army but not the meaning of exclusive command; if this holds for war, it should hold for sacrifice as well.
translations.idiomatic: The Heir Apparent has the duty of pacifying the army but not the authority of exclusive command; if this holds for war, it should hold for sacrifice as well.

sentences.zh: 案祭統，『夫祭之道，孫為王父尸』。

translations.literal: Considering the Record of Sacrifice: 'The way of sacrifice— the grandson serves as impersonator for his grandfather.'
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Sacrifice states: 'The way of sacrifice— the grandson serves as impersonator for his grandfather.'

sentences.zh: 又云，『祭有昭穆，所以別父子』。

translations.literal: It also says: 'In sacrifice there is zhao and mu, by which father and son are distinguished.'
translations.idiomatic: It also states: 'In sacrifice there are zhao and mu positions, by which father and son are distinguished.'

sentences.zh: 太子監國，雖不攝，至於宗廟，則昭穆實存，謂事不可亂。

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent supervises the state; although he does not act as regent, as to the ancestral temple, zhao and mu truly exist— I hold that the affair cannot be confused.
translations.idiomatic: The Heir Apparent supervises the state; although he does not act as regent, as to the ancestral temple zhao and mu truly exist—I hold that the affair cannot be confused.

sentences.zh: 又云，『有故則使人』。

translations.literal: It also says: 'When there is cause, then send someone.'
translations.idiomatic: It also states: 'When there is cause, one sends another in one's place.'

sentences.zh: 准此二三，太子無奉祀之道。

translations.literal: Based on these two or three points, the Heir Apparent has no way of performing sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Based on these points, the Heir Apparent has no proper way of performing sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 又皇女夭札，則實同宮一體之哀，理不得異。

translations.literal: Moreover, the imperial daughter's early death is truly the same grief as one body within the palace— in principle it cannot differ.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the imperial daughter's early death is truly grief shared as one body within the palace—in principle it cannot be treated differently.

sentences.zh: 設令得祀，令猶無親奉之義。

translations.literal: Even supposing sacrifice were permitted, the edict still has no meaning of personal attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Even supposing sacrifice were permitted, the edict still carries no meaning of personal attendance.

sentences.zh: 」博士郁議：「案春秋，太子奉社稷之粢盛，長子主器，出可守宗廟，以為祭主，易彖明文。

translations.literal: " Erudite Yu deliberated: "Considering the Spring and Autumn Annals, the Heir Apparent presents the sacrificial grain of the state altars; the eldest son holds the vessel; going forth he may guard the ancestral temple and serve as sacrifice master— the Commentary on the Changes states this explicitly.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Yu argued: "The Spring and Autumn Annals records that the Heir Apparent presents the sacrificial grain of the state altars; the eldest son holds the vessel; going forth he may guard the ancestral temple and serve as sacrifice master—the Commentary on the Changes states this explicitly.

sentences.zh: 監國之重，居然親祭。

translations.literal: The weight of supervising the state naturally entails personal sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The weighty duty of supervising the state naturally requires personal sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 皇女夭札，時既同宮，三月廢祭，於禮宜停。

translations.literal: The imperial daughter's early death— the time being within the same palace— sacrifices are suspended for three months; in ritual it should stop.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial daughter's early death occurred within the same palace; sacrifices should be suspended for three months—in ritual terms the rites should stop.

sentences.zh: 」二議不同。

translations.literal: " The two deliberations differ.
translations.idiomatic: The two deliberations differed.

sentences.zh: 尚書參議，宜以郁議為允。

translations.literal: The Ministry deliberated and held Yu's deliberation acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry reviewed the matter and held Yu's deliberation acceptable.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 大明三年十一月乙丑朔，有司奏：「四時廟祠，吉日已定，遇雨及舉哀，舊停親奉，以有司行事。

translations.literal: On the first day yichou of the eleventh month of the third year of Daming, the responsible officials memorialized: "The auspicious days for the four seasonal temple sacrifices have been fixed; when rain occurs or mourning is observed, personal attendance has formerly been suspended and the responsible officials perform the rites.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day yichou of the eleventh month in the third year of Daming, the responsible officials memorialized: "The auspicious days for the four seasonal temple sacrifices have been fixed; when rain occurs or mourning is observed, personal attendance has formerly been suspended and the responsible officials perform the rites.

sentences.zh: 先下使禮官博議，於禮為得遷日與不？

translations.literal: First order the ritual officers to deliberate broadly— in ritual is it proper to postpone the day or not?
translations.idiomatic: First order the ritual officers to deliberate broadly—according to ritual, is it proper to postpone the day or not?

sentences.zh: 」博士江長議：「禮記祭統：『君之祭也，有故則使人，而君不失其儀。

translations.literal: " Erudite Jiang Chang deliberated: "The Record of Sacrifice in the Book of Rites: 'When the lord sacrifices, if there is cause then he sends someone, yet the lord does not lose his propriety.'
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Jiang Chang argued: "The Record of Sacrifice in the Book of Rites states: 'When the lord sacrifices, if there is cause then he sends someone, yet the lord does not lose his propriety.'

sentences.zh: 』鄭玄云：『君雖不親，祭禮無闕，君德不損。

translations.literal: ' Zheng Xuan says: 'Although the lord does not attend in person, the sacrificial ritual is not lacking and the lord's virtue is not diminished.'
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan says: 'Although the lord does not attend in person, the sacrificial ritual is not lacking and the lord's virtue is not diminished.'

sentences.zh: 』愚以為有故則必使人者，明無遷移之文。

translations.literal: ' In my humble view, that when there is cause one must send someone shows clearly that there is no text for postponement.
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view, that when there is cause one must send someone shows clearly that there is no text authorizing postponement.

sentences.zh: 苟有司充事，謂不宜改日。

translations.literal: If the responsible officials can fulfill the affair, I hold that the day should not be changed.
translations.idiomatic: If the responsible officials can complete the rites, I hold that the day ought not be changed.

sentences.zh: 」太常丞陸澄議：「案周禮宗伯之職，『若王不與祭祀則攝位』。

translations.literal: " Vice Director of Ceremonies Lu Cheng deliberated: "Considering the duties of the Ritual Master in the Rites of Zhou: 'If the king does not join the sacrifice, then [the minister] takes his place.'
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Lu Cheng argued: "The Rites of Zhou assigns the Ritual Master: 'If the king does not join the sacrifice, then [the minister] takes his place.'

sentences.zh: 鄭君曰：『王有故，行其祭事也。

translations.literal: Master Zheng says: 'The king has cause; [the minister] performs the sacrificial affair.'
translations.idiomatic: Master Zheng says: 'When the king has cause, the minister performs the sacrificial rites.'

sentences.zh: 』臣以為此謂在致齋，祭事盡備，神不可瀆，齋不可久，而王有他故，則使有司攝焉。

translations.literal: ' Your subject holds that this refers to when, during the period of fasting, all sacrificial preparations are complete— the spirits cannot be profaned, fasting cannot be prolonged, and when the king has other cause, he has the responsible officials act in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject holds that this refers to when, during the period of fasting, all sacrificial preparations are complete—the spirits cannot be profaned, fasting cannot be prolonged, and when the king has other cause, he has the responsible officials act in his stead.

sentences.zh: 晉泰始七年四月，世祖將親祠于太廟。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the seventh year of Taishi under Jin, Emperor Shizu was about to sacrifice in person at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the seventh year of Taishi under Jin, Emperor Shizu was preparing to sacrifice in person at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，車駕夕牲。

translations.literal: On gengxu, the imperial carriage inspected the sacrificial victims in the evening.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengxu day, the emperor inspected the sacrificial victims in the evening.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，雨。

translations.literal: On xinhai, it rained.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinhai day, rain fell.

sentences.zh: 有司行事。

translations.literal: The responsible officials performed the rites.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible officials carried out the rites.

sentences.zh: 此雖非人故，蓋亦天硋也。

translations.literal: Although this was not human cause, it was perhaps heaven's obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: Although this was not a human cause, it was perhaps heaven's obstruction.

sentences.zh: 求之古禮，未乖周制。

translations.literal: Seeking in ancient ritual, it does not violate Zhou practice.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking guidance in ancient ritual, this does not violate Zhou practice.

sentences.zh: 案禮記，『孔子答曾子，當祭而日蝕太廟火，如牲至未殺，則廢』。

translations.literal: Considering the Book of Rites: 'Confucius answered Zengzi: when sacrificing, if there is an eclipse or fire in the Imperial Ancestral Temple, if the victims have arrived but not yet been slaughtered, then the sacrifice is cancelled.'
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Rites records: 'Confucius answered Zengzi: when sacrificing, if there is an eclipse or fire in the Imperial Ancestral Temple, if the victims have arrived but not yet been slaughtered, then the sacrifice is cancelled.'

sentences.zh: 然則祭非無可廢之道也。

translations.literal: Thus sacrifice is not without grounds for cancellation.
translations.idiomatic: Thus sacrifice is not without grounds on which it may be cancelled.

sentences.zh: 但權所為之輕重耳。

translations.literal: It is only a matter of the lightness or weight of provisional action.
translations.idiomatic: It is only a question of how lightly or heavily one acts provisionally.

sentences.zh: 日蝕廟火，變之甚者，故乃牲至尚猶可廢。

translations.literal: Eclipse and temple fire are extremely severe changes; even when the victims have arrived, cancellation is still possible.
translations.idiomatic: Eclipse and temple fire are the most severe of portents; even when the victims have already arrived, cancellation remains possible.

sentences.zh: 推此而降，可以理尋。

translations.literal: Extrapolating downward from this, the principle can be traced.
translations.idiomatic: Extrapolating downward from this, the underlying principle becomes clear.

sentences.zh: 今散齋之內，未及致齋，而有輕哀甚雨，日時展事，可以延敬。

translations.literal: Now, within the period of general fasting, before entering the period of strict fasting, if there is light mourning or heavy rain, the scheduled affair can be postponed out of reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Now, within the period of general fasting, before entering strict fasting, if there is light mourning or heavy rain, the scheduled affair can be postponed out of reverence.

sentences.zh: 不愆義情，無傷正典，改擇令日，夫何以疑。

translations.literal: Without violating ritual sentiment, without harming the canonical rite, choosing an auspicious day— why doubt?
translations.idiomatic: Without violating ritual sentiment or harming the canonical rite, choosing an auspicious day—why hesitate?

sentences.zh: 愚謂散齋而有舉哀若雨，可更遷日。

translations.literal: In my humble view, if during general fasting there is mourning or rain, the day may be changed.
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view, if during general fasting there is mourning or rain, the day may be postponed.

sentences.zh: 唯入致齋及日月逼晚者，乃使有司行事耳。

translations.literal: Only when entering strict fasting and when the sun and moon press late should the responsible officials perform the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Only when one enters strict fasting, or when the day grows late, should the responsible officials perform the rites.

sentences.zh: 又前代司空顧和啟，南郊車駕已出遇雨，宜遷日更郊，事見施用。

translations.literal: Also, in a former generation Minister of Works Gu He submitted that when the southern suburban carriage had already departed and encountered rain, the day should be changed and the suburban sacrifice repeated— the affair was seen and applied.
translations.idiomatic: Also, in a former generation Minister of Works Gu He submitted that when the southern suburban carriage had already departed and encountered rain, the day should be changed and the suburban sacrifice repeated—the proposal was adopted.

sentences.zh: 郊之與廟，其敬可均，至日猶遷，況散齋邪。

translations.literal: Suburban and temple rites are equally reverent; if even on the day of arrival postponement is made, how much more so during general fasting?
translations.idiomatic: Suburban and temple rites are equally reverent; if even on the day of arrival postponement is permitted, how much more so during general fasting?

sentences.zh: 」殿中郎殷淡議：「曾子問『日蝕太廟火，牲未殺則廢』。

translations.literal: " Palace Attendant Yin Dan deliberated: "Zengzi asked: 'If there is an eclipse or fire in the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and the victims have not yet been slaughtered, then cancel.'
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Yin Dan argued: "Zengzi asked: 'If there is an eclipse or fire in the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and the victims have not yet been slaughtered, then cancel.'

sentences.zh: 縱有故則使人。

translations.literal: Even when there is cause, then send someone.
translations.idiomatic: Even when there is cause, one sends another in one's place.

sentences.zh: 清廟敬重，郊禋禮大，故廟焚日蝕，許以可遷；

translations.literal: The Clear Temple is reverently weighty; suburban and feng rites are great— therefore when the temple burns or the sun eclipses, postponement is permitted;
translations.idiomatic: The Clear Temple is reverently weighty; suburban and feng rites are great—therefore when the temple burns or the sun eclipses, postponement is permitted;

sentences.zh: 輕哀微故，事不合改。

translations.literal: light mourning and minor cause do not accord with change.
translations.idiomatic: light mourning and minor cause do not warrant change.

sentences.zh: 是以鼷鼠食牛，改卜非禮。

translations.literal: Therefore when a mouse ate the ox, changing the divination was unritual.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore when a mouse ate the ox, changing the divination was contrary to ritual.

sentences.zh: 晉世祖有司行事，顧司空之改郊月，既不見其當時之宜，此不足為准。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu of Jin had the responsible officials perform the rites, and Minister Gu changed the suburban month— the appropriateness of that time is not seen; this cannot serve as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu of Jin had the responsible officials perform the rites, and Minister Gu changed the suburban month—the appropriateness of that time is not evident; this cannot serve as precedent.

sentences.zh: 愚謂日蝕廟火，天譴之變，廼可遷日。

translations.literal: In my humble view, eclipse and temple fire are heaven's reproof— only then may the day be changed.
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view, eclipse and temple fire are heaven's reproof—only then may the day be changed.

sentences.zh: 至於舉哀小故，不宜改辰。

translations.literal: As for light mourning and minor cause, the day should not be changed.
translations.idiomatic: As for light mourning and minor cause, the day ought not be changed.

sentences.zh: 」眾議不同。

translations.literal: " The collective deliberations differ.
translations.idiomatic: The collective deliberations differed.

sentences.zh: 參議，既有理據，且晉氏遷郊，宋初遷祠，並有成准。

translations.literal: Upon comparison, since there are grounds in principle, and since Jin postponed the suburban sacrifice and Song at the beginning postponed the temple sacrifice, both have established precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Upon review, since there are grounds in principle, and since Jin postponed the suburban sacrifice and early Song postponed the temple sacrifice, both have established precedents.

sentences.zh: 謂孟月散齋之中，遇雨及舉輕哀，宜擇吉更遷，無定限數。

translations.literal: I hold that during general fasting in the first month of the season, if rain occurs or light mourning is observed, an auspicious day should be chosen for postponement, with no fixed limit on number.
translations.idiomatic: During general fasting in the first month of the season, if rain occurs or light mourning is observed, an auspicious day should be chosen for postponement, with no fixed limit on number.

sentences.zh: 唯入致齋及侵仲月節者，使有司行事。

translations.literal: Only when entering strict fasting and encroaching on the middle month of the season should the responsible officials perform the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Only when one enters strict fasting and encroaches on the middle month of the season should the responsible officials perform the rites.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 大明五年十月甲寅，有司奏：「今月八日烝祠二廟，公卿行事。

translations.literal: On the jiayin day of the tenth month of the fifth year of Daming, the responsible officials memorialized: "On the eighth day of this month, winter sacrifice will be offered at the two temples; the dukes and ministers will perform the rites.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiayin day of the tenth month in the fifth year of Daming, the responsible officials memorialized: "On the eighth day of this month, winter sacrifice will be offered at the two temples, with the dukes and ministers performing the rites.

sentences.zh: 有皇太子獻妃服。

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent has mourning garments for his consort.
translations.idiomatic: The Heir Apparent is in mourning garments for his consort.

sentences.zh: 」前太常丞庾蔚之議：「禮所以有喪廢祭，由祭必有樂。

translations.literal: " Former Vice Director of Ceremonies Yu Weizhi deliberated: "The reason ritual suspends sacrifice during mourning is that sacrifice must have music.
translations.idiomatic: Former Vice Director Yu Weizhi argued: "The reason ritual suspends sacrifice during mourning is that sacrifice must have music.

sentences.zh: 皇太子以元嫡之重，故主上服妃，不以尊降。

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent, by the weight of being the primary consort's husband, therefore has the sovereign wear mourning for the consort without lowering rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Heir Apparent, by the weight of being the primary consort's husband, therefore requires the sovereign to wear mourning for the consort without lowering rank.

sentences.zh: 既正服大功，愚謂不應祭。

translations.literal: Having already donned proper major mourning garments, I hold that sacrifice should not be performed.
translations.idiomatic: Having already donned proper major mourning garments, I hold that sacrifice ought not be performed.

sentences.zh: 有故，三公行事，是得祭之辰，非今之比。

translations.literal: When there is cause, the Three Excellencies perform the rites— that is a time when sacrifice may proceed; it is not comparable to the present case.
translations.idiomatic: When there is cause, the Three Excellencies perform the rites—that is a time when sacrifice may proceed; it is not comparable to the present case.

sentences.zh: 卿卒猶不繹，況於太子妃乎？

translations.literal: When a minister dies, even the yi-sacrifice is not performed; how much more so for the Heir Apparent's consort?
translations.idiomatic: When a minister dies, even the yi-sacrifice is suspended; how much more so for the Heir Apparent's consort?

sentences.zh: 」博士司馬興之議：「夫緦則不祭，禮之大經。

translations.literal: " Erudite Sima Xingzhi argued: "When in zi-mourning one does not sacrifice— that is a great principle of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Sima Xingzhi argued: "When in zi-mourning one does not sacrifice—that is a great principle of ritual.

sentences.zh: 卿卒不繹，春秋明義。

translations.literal: When a minister dies the yi-sacrifice is not performed— the Spring and Autumn Annals makes the meaning clear.
translations.idiomatic: When a minister dies the yi-sacrifice is not performed—the Spring and Autumn Annals makes the meaning clear.

sentences.zh: 又尋魏代平原公主薨，高堂隆議不應三月廢祠，而猶云殯葬之間，權廢事改吉，芬馥享祠。

translations.literal: Furthermore, when the Princess of Pingyuan died in Wei, Gao Tanglong argued that the three-month suspension of sacrifice should not apply, yet still said that between interment and burial the rites might be provisionally suspended and a propitious day chosen, after which fragrant sacrifice might resume.
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, when the Princess of Pingyuan died in Wei, Gao Tanglong argued that the three-month suspension of sacrifice should not apply, yet still held that between interment and burial the rites might be provisionally suspended and a propitious day chosen, after which fragrant sacrifice could resume.

sentences.zh: 尋此語意，非使有司。

translations.literal: Seeking the meaning of these words, they do not authorize having the responsible officials perform the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking the meaning of these words, they do not authorize the responsible officials to perform the rites.

sentences.zh: 此無服之喪，尚以未葬為廢，況皇太子妃及大功未祔者邪？

translations.literal: Even for mourning without required garments, suspension before burial is still observed— how much more for the Heir Apparent's consort and one in major mourning not yet enshrined?
translations.idiomatic: Even for mourning without required garments, suspension before burial is still observed—how much more for the Heir Apparent's consort and one in major mourning not yet enshrined?

sentences.zh: 上尋禮文，下准前代，不得烝祠。

translations.literal: Consulting ritual texts above and comparing with former dynasties below, winter sacrifice cannot be performed.
translations.idiomatic: Consulting ritual texts above and comparing with former dynasties below, winter sacrifice cannot be held.

sentences.zh: 」領軍長史周景遠議：「案禮『緦不祭』。

translations.literal: " Director of the Headquarters Staff Zhou Jingyuan argued: "The Rites state: 'In zi-mourning one does not sacrifice.'
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Headquarters Staff Zhou Jingyuan argued: "The Rites state: 'In zi-mourning one does not sacrifice.'

sentences.zh: 大功廢祠，理不俟言。

translations.literal: That major mourning suspends sacrifice needs no further argument.
translations.idiomatic: That major mourning suspends sacrifice requires no further argument.

sentences.zh: 今皇太子故妃既未山塋，未從權制，則應依禮廢烝嘗。

translations.literal: Now that the Heir Apparent's deceased consort has not yet been buried in the mountain tomb and provisional regulations have not been applied, winter and seasonal sacrifice should be suspended according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the Heir Apparent's deceased consort has not yet been buried in the mountain tomb and provisional regulations have not been applied, winter and seasonal sacrifice ought to be suspended according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 至尊以大功之服，於禮不得親奉，非有故之謂，亦不使公卿行事。

translations.literal: The sovereign in major mourning garments cannot personally attend according to ritual; this is not a case of "cause," and neither should the dukes and ministers perform the rites.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign, wearing major mourning garments, cannot personally attend according to ritual; this is not a case of "cause," and neither should the dukes and ministers perform the rites.

sentences.zh: 」右丞徐爰議以為：「禮，『緦不祭』，蓋惟通議。

translations.literal: " Right Assistant Director Xu Ai argued: "The Rites' statement 'in zi-mourning one does not sacrifice' is surely only a general principle.
translations.idiomatic: Right Assistant Director Xu Ai argued: "The Rites' statement 'in zi-mourning one does not sacrifice' is surely only a general principle.

sentences.zh: 大夫以尊貴降絕，及其有服，不容復異。

translations.literal: Grand officers, by their exalted rank having reduced mourning obligations, when they do observe mourning garments cannot be treated differently.
translations.idiomatic: Grand officers, by their exalted rank having reduced mourning obligations, when they do observe mourning garments cannot be treated differently from others.

sentences.zh: 祭統云『君有故使人可』者，謂於禮應祭，君不得齋，祭不可闕，故使臣下攝奉。

translations.literal: The Record of Sacrifice says 'when the lord has cause, sending someone is permitted'— this means when ritual requires sacrifice, the lord cannot keep the fast, and the sacrifice must not be omitted, so ministers perform it on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Sacrifice says 'when the lord has cause, sending someone is permitted'—this means when ritual requires sacrifice, the lord cannot keep the fast, and the sacrifice must not be omitted, so ministers perform it on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 不謂君不應祭，有司行事也。

translations.literal: It does not mean that when the lord should not sacrifice, the responsible officials perform the rites.
translations.idiomatic: It does not mean that when the lord should not sacrifice, the responsible officials may perform the rites in his stead.

sentences.zh: 晉咸寧四年，景獻皇后崩，晉武帝伯母，宗廟廢一時之祀，雖名號尊崇，粗可依准。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianning under Jin, when Empress Jingxian died— aunt to Emperor Wu of Jin— temple sacrifice was suspended for a time; although her title was exalted, this may roughly serve as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xianning under Jin, when Empress Jingxian died— aunt to Emperor Wu of Jin— temple sacrifice was suspended for a time; although her title was exalted, this may serve roughly as precedent.

sentences.zh: 今太子妃至尊正服大功，非有故之比。

translations.literal: Now the Heir Apparent's consort requires the sovereign to wear proper major mourning garments— not comparable to a case of "cause."
translations.idiomatic: Now the Heir Apparent's consort requires the sovereign to wear proper major mourning garments—not comparable to a case of "cause."

sentences.zh: 既未山塋，謂烝祠宜廢。

translations.literal: Since burial in the mountain tomb has not yet occurred, winter sacrifice should be suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Since burial in the mountain tomb has not yet occurred, winter sacrifice ought to be suspended.

sentences.zh: 尋蔚之等議，指歸不殊，闕烝為允。

translations.literal: Reviewing the deliberations of Yu Weizhi and others, their conclusions do not differ— omitting winter sacrifice is appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing the deliberations of Yu Weizhi and others, their conclusions do not differ—omitting winter sacrifice is appropriate.

sentences.zh: 過卒哭祔廟，一依常典。

translations.literal: After zucu and enshrinement in the temple, follow the regular canon.
translations.idiomatic: After zucu and enshrinement in the temple, one follows the regular canon.

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: " An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 」太學博士虞龢議：「檢周禮，四時講武獻牲，各有所施。

translations.idiomatic: Erudite Yu He of the Imperial Academy argued: "Examining the Rites of Zhou, the four seasonal military reviews with sacrificial victims each have their proper application.

sentences.zh: 振旅春蒐，則以祭社；

translations.literal: When troops are reviewed in spring during the sou hunt, sacrifice is offered at the altar of Earth;
translations.idiomatic: When troops are reviewed in spring during the sou hunt, sacrifice is offered at the Altar of Earth;

sentences.zh: 茇舍夏苗，則以享礿；

translations.literal: when encamped in summer during the miao hunt, the luo offering is performed;
translations.idiomatic: when encamped in summer during the miao hunt, the luo offering is made;

sentences.zh: 治兵秋獮，則以祀祊；

translations.literal: when troops are marshaled in autumn during the xian hunt, sacrifice is offered at the altar of the war-god;
translations.idiomatic: when troops are marshaled in autumn during the xian hunt, sacrifice is offered at the Altar of the War-God;

sentences.zh: 大閱冬狩，則以享烝。

translations.literal: when the great review is held in winter during the shou hunt, the zheng offering is performed.
translations.idiomatic: when the great review is held in winter during the shou hunt, the zheng offering is made.

sentences.zh: 案漢祭祀志：『唯立秋之日，白郊事畢，始揚威武，名曰「貙劉」。

translations.literal: Examining the Han Treatise on Sacrifice: 'Only on the day of the Beginning of Autumn, after the white suburban rite is complete, martial prowess is displayed— called "the leopard hunt."
translations.idiomatic: Examining the Han Treatise on Sacrifice: 'Only on the day of the Beginning of Autumn, after the white suburban rite is complete, martial prowess is displayed—called "the leopard hunt."

sentences.zh: 乘輿入囿，躬執弩以射，牲以鹿麑。

sentences.zh: 太宰令謁者各一人，載獲車馳送陵廟。

translations.literal: The Director of Victims and the Attendant each in one carriage, carrying the game obtained, rush to deliver them to the imperial tombs and temples.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Victims and the Attendant, each in one carriage and carrying the game obtained, rush to deliver them to the imperial tombs and temples.

translations.idiomatic: Concurrent Director of Ceremonies Yu Weizhi argued: "What He said concerns conducting hunts and reviews at the proper season—this rite has long been abandoned.

translations.idiomatic: Have the ritual officers deliberate the matter broadly.

sentences.zh: 伏尋三年之制，自天子達。

translations.literal: Examining the three-year rule, it extends from the Son of Heaven downward.
translations.idiomatic: Examining the three-year rule, it extends from the Son of Heaven down through all ranks.

sentences.zh: 漢文愍秦餘之弊，於是制為權典。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Han, pitying the abuses left by Qin, therefore established a provisional canon.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han, pitying the abuses left by Qin, therefore established a provisional mourning canon.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉以來，卒哭而祔則就吉。

translations.literal: From Wei and Jin onward, when zucu and enshrinement occur mourning ends and auspicious rites resume.
translations.idiomatic: From Wei and Jin onward, when zucu and enshrinement occur, mourning ends and auspicious rites resume.

sentences.zh: 案禮記王制，『三年不祭，唯祭天地社稷，為越紼而行事』。

translations.literal: Examining the Royal Regulations in the Book of Rites: 'For three years one does not sacrifice, except to Heaven, Earth, and the altars of soil and grain, crossing the mourning cord to perform these affairs.'
translations.idiomatic: Examining the Royal Regulations in the Book of Rites: 'For three years one does not sacrifice, except to Heaven, Earth, and the altars of soil and grain—crossing the mourning cord to perform these affairs.'

sentences.zh: 鄭玄云：『唯不敢以卑廢尊也。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan says: 'This is only because one dares not let the low displace the high.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan says: 'This is only because one dares not let what is low displace what is high.

sentences.zh: 』范宣難杜預、段暢，所以闕宗廟祭者，皆人理所奉，哀戚之情，同於生者。

translations.literal: ' Fan Xuan challenged Du Yu and Duan Chang; the reason ancestral temple sacrifice is omitted is that all are objects of human devotion— grief and sorrow are the same as toward the living.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Xuan challenged Du Yu and Duan Chang; the reason ancestral temple sacrifice is omitted is that all are objects of human devotion—grief and sorrow are the same as toward the living.

sentences.zh: 譙周祭志稱：『禮，身有喪，則不為吉祭。

translations.literal: Qiao Zhou's Treatise on Sacrifice states: 'By ritual, when one is in mourning one does not perform auspicious sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zhou's Treatise on Sacrifice states: 'By ritual, when one is in mourning one does not perform auspicious sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 緦麻之喪，於祖考有服者，則亦不祭，為神不饗也。

translations.literal: In zi and ma mourning, toward forebears to whom one owes mourning garments, one also does not sacrifice, because the spirits will not accept the offering.
translations.idiomatic: In zi and ma mourning, toward forebears to whom one owes mourning garments, one also does not sacrifice, for the spirits will not accept the offering.

sentences.zh: 』尋宮中有故，雖在無服，亦廢祭三月，有喪不祭。

translations.literal: ' Examining further: when there is cause within the palace, even without required mourning garments sacrifice is suspended for three months— mourning means no sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Examining further: when there is cause within the palace, even without required mourning garments sacrifice is suspended for three months—mourning means no sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 如或非若三年之內必宜親奉者，則應禘序昭穆。

translations.literal: If within the three years personal attendance were truly required, then di and xia should order zhao and mu.
translations.idiomatic: If within the three years personal attendance were truly required, then di and xia should arrange zhao and mu.

sentences.zh: 而今必須免喪，然後禘祫，故知未祭之意，當似可思。

translations.literal: Yet now di and xia must wait until mourning ends— therefore one knows the meaning of not yet sacrificing should be considered.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now di and xia must wait until mourning ends—therefore one knows the meaning of not yet sacrificing should be considered.

sentences.zh: 起居注，晉武有二喪，兩朞之中，並不自祠。

translations.literal: The Daily Records show that Emperor Wu of Jin had two mourning obligations and during both periods did not personally sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The Daily Records show that Emperor Wu of Jin had two mourning obligations and during both periods did not sacrifice in person.

sentences.zh: 亦近代前事也。

translations.literal: This too is a recent precedent.
translations.idiomatic: This too is a precedent from recent times.

sentences.zh: 伏惟至尊孝越姬文，情深明發，公服雖釋，純哀內纏。

translations.literal: The sovereign's filial piety surpasses that of King Wen of Zhou; his affection is deep and clearly expressed; although public mourning garments are removed, pure grief remains inwardly bound.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign's filial piety surpasses that of King Wen of Zhou; his affection runs deep and is clearly expressed; although public mourning garments are removed, pure grief remains inwardly bound.

sentences.zh: 推訪典例，則未應親奉。

translations.literal: Seeking precedents in the canon, personal attendance should not yet occur.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking precedents in the canon, personal attendance ought not yet occur.

sentences.zh: 有司祗應，祭不為曠。

translations.idiomatic: The responsible officials reverently performing the rites—sacrifice is not neglected.

translations.idiomatic: I hold that Empress Dowager Zhao's wine cup may be entrusted to the responsible officials to present.

translations.idiomatic: Six hundred sixty-three officials of the second rank took part in the deliberation.
