translations.literal: Grand Tutor Prince Jiangxia Yigong argued: "The classics are damaged and forged; teachings and transmissions diverge in many schools— those who speak with certainty are few, and those who truly investigate are rare.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Prince Jiangxia Yigong argued: "The classics are damaged and forged; teachings and transmissions diverge in many schools—those who speak with certainty are few, and those who truly investigate are rare.

translations.literal: Thus the debate over the Six Ancestors went astray among eclectic scholars; the alternating theories of destruction and preservation confused the many schools.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the debate over the Six Ancestors went astray among eclectic scholars, and the alternating theories of destruction and preservation confused the many schools.

sentences.zh: 章皇太后誕神啟聖，禮備中興，慶流胙胤，德光義遠。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Zhang gave birth to the divine and opened the sage era; ritual was complete at the restoration; blessings flowed to enfeoffed descendants; virtue shone and righteousness reached far.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Zhang gave birth to the divine and opened the sage era; ritual was complete at the restoration; blessings flowed to enfeoffed descendants; her virtue shone and her righteousness reached far.

translations.literal: She should be honored through the ages with enduring fragrance, a model passed down through generations.
translations.idiomatic: She should be honored through the ages with enduring fragrance, a model passed down from generation to generation.

translations.idiomatic: How can she be lowered to equal ordinary ranks and made to follow the regular canon instead?

translations.idiomatic: Examining the Book of Rites on not substituting in sacrifice, extending even to the loving mother—the wording shows where it applies.

translations.literal: Guliang on "the grandson stops" distinguishes the lord who establishes sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In Guliang's commentary on "the grandson stops," one distinguishes the lord who establishes sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 則親執虔祀，事異前志。

translations.literal: Thus personal attendance in reverent sacrifice differs from earlier records.
translations.idiomatic: Thus personal attendance in reverent sacrifice differs from what earlier records prescribe.

sentences.zh: 將由大君之宜，其職彌重，人極之貴，其數特中。

translations.literal: This arises from the exalted sovereign's proper role— the duty is all the heavier; the pinnacle of human honor— the number stands specially in the middle.

translations.idiomatic: Moreover Han's grand tradition ascended to paired enshrinement, and Jin's clear regulations all retained sacrificial offering.

translations.idiomatic: What is cited from Gongyang only strengthens obstinate adherence to one view.

translations.idiomatic: How can one equal emperors in rank yet follow gentry and commoners in sacrifice—seeking regulations by sentiment, the inversion grows ever worse.

translations.idiomatic: Examining the Rites: a wife has no canon of appearing before an elder brother; Empress Dowager Zhao's position is collateral honor—complete reverence in ritual cannot be required.

translations.idiomatic: For Emperor Xiaowu and Empress Dowager Zhao's two chambers—victims and offerings should be omitted.

translations.idiomatic: Director of Ceremonies Yu Yuan argued: "Zheng and chang sacrifice—the affair exists for continuing the line; therefore though collateral honor is near, younger brothers and nephews do not sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 君道雖高，臣無祭典。

translations.literal: Though the way of the lord is exalted, a minister has no canon of sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Though the way of the lord is exalted, a minister has no canonical rite of sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 按晉景帝之於武帝，屬居伯父，武帝至祭之日，猶進觴爵。

translations.literal: Examining Emperor Jing of Jin toward Emperor Wu— relation was paternal uncle— on Emperor Wu's sacrifice day he still advanced the wine cup.
translations.idiomatic: Examining Emperor Jing of Jin toward Emperor Wu—relation was paternal uncle—on Emperor Wu's sacrifice day he still advanced the wine cup.

sentences.zh: 今上既纂祠文皇，於孝武室謂宜進拜而已，觴爵使有司行事。

translations.literal: Now the sovereign having succeeded in sacrificing to Emperor Wen— at Emperor Xiaowu's chamber should only advance bow; the wine cup should have the responsible officials perform the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Now the sovereign having succeeded in sacrificing to Emperor Wen—at Emperor Xiaowu's chamber should only advance bow; the wine cup should have the responsible officials perform the rites.

sentences.zh: 按禮『過墓則軾，過祀則下』。

translations.literal: Examining the Rites: 'When passing a tomb lean on the crossbar; when passing a place of sacrifice dismount.
translations.idiomatic: Examining the Rites: 'When passing a tomb, lean on the crossbar; when passing a place of sacrifice, dismount.

sentences.zh: 凡在神祇，尚或致恭；

translations.literal: ' For all spirit beings reverence may still be shown;
translations.idiomatic: For all spirit beings reverence may still be shown;

sentences.zh: 況昭太后母臨四海，至尊親曾北面，兄母有敬，謂宜進拜，祝文宜稱皇帝諱。

translations.literal: how much more Empress Dowager Zhao who as mother faced the realm— the sovereign once personally faced north; elder brother's mother deserves reverence— should advance to bow; the prayer text should use the emperor's taboo name.
translations.idiomatic: how much more Empress Dowager Zhao who as mother faced the realm—the sovereign once personally faced north; elder brother's mother deserves reverence—should advance to bow; the prayer text should use the emperor's taboo name.

sentences.zh: 尋皇后廟見之禮，本修虔為義，今於孝武，論其嫂叔，則無通問之典，語其尊卑，亦無相見之義。

translations.literal: Examining the empress's temple appearance ritual— originally the meaning is cultivating reverence; as to Emperor Xiaowu, discussing sister-in-law and younger brother-in-law— no canon of communication; discussing rank— no meaning of mutual appearance.
translations.idiomatic: Examining the empress's temple appearance ritual—originally the meaning is cultivating reverence; as to Emperor Xiaowu, discussing sister-in-law and younger brother-in-law—no canon of communication; discussing rank—no meaning of mutual appearance.

sentences.zh: 又皇后登御之初，昭后猶正位在宮，敬謁之道，久已前備。

translations.literal: Also when the empress first ascended, Empress Dowager Zhao still held orthodox position in the palace— the path of reverent audience was long since prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Also when the empress first ascended, Empress Dowager Zhao still held orthodox position in the palace—the path of reverent audience was long since prepared.

sentences.zh: 愚謂孝武、昭太后二室，並不復薦告。

translations.literal: I hold Emperor Xiaowu and Empress Dowager Zhao's two chambers should both omit offering and announcement.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that Emperor Xiaowu and Empress Dowager Zhao's two chambers should both omit offering and announcement.

sentences.zh: 」參議以愿議為允。

translations.literal: " Upon joint deliberation Yu Yuan's view was held acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Upon joint deliberation Yu Yuan's view was held acceptable.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝元徽二年十月壬寅，有司奏昭太后廟毀置。

translations.literal: On the renyin day of the tenth month of the second year of Yuanhui under the deposed Emperor, the responsible officials memorialized on destroying and relocating the temple of Empress Dowager Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: On the renyin day of the tenth month in the second year of Yuanhui under the deposed Emperor, the responsible officials memorialized on destroying and relocating the temple of Empress Dowager Zhao.

sentences.zh: 下禮官詳議。

translations.literal: Refer to the ritual officers for detailed deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Refer the matter to the ritual officers for detailed deliberation.

sentences.zh: 太常丞韓賁議：「按君母之尊，義發春秋，庶後饗薦無間。

translations.literal: Director of Ceremonies Han Ben argued: "Examining the exaltation of the lord's mother— meaning arises from the Spring and Autumn Annals; offerings to secondary consorts are uninterrupted.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Ceremonies Han Ben argued: "Examining the exaltation of the lord's mother—meaning arises from the Spring and Autumn Annals; offerings to secondary consorts are uninterrupted.

sentences.zh: 周典七廟承統，猶親盡則毀。

translations.literal: The Zhou canon of seven temples inheriting the line— yet when kinship is exhausted destruction follows.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou canon of seven temples inheriting the line—yet when kinship is exhausted destruction follows.

sentences.zh: 況伯之所生，而無服代祭，稽之前代，未見其準。

translations.literal: How much more one born of a paternal uncle— no mourning garments, no generation serving sacrifice— seeking precedent in former ages, none is seen.
translations.idiomatic: How much more one born of a paternal uncle—no mourning garments, no generation serving sacrifice—seeking precedent in former ages, none is seen.

sentences.zh: 」都令史殷匪子議：「昭皇太后不係於祖宗，進退宜毀。

translations.literal: " Chief Clerk Yin Feizi argued: "Empress Dowager Zhao is not tied to the ancestors— entering and leaving should mean destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Yin Feizi argued: "Empress Dowager Zhao is not tied to the ancestors—entering and leaving should mean destruction.

sentences.zh: 議者云，『妾祔於妾祖姑』，祔既必告，毀不容異。

translations.literal: Deliberators say: 'A concubine enshrined with her husband's concubine-grandmother'— if enshrinement requires announcement, destruction cannot differ.
translations.idiomatic: Deliberators say: 'A concubine enshrined with her husband's concubine-grandmother'—if enshrinement requires announcement, destruction cannot differ.

sentences.zh: 應告章皇太后一室。

translations.literal: Announcement should be made at Empress Dowager Zhang's chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Announcement should be made at the chamber of Empress Dowager Zhang.

sentences.zh: 按記云：『妾祔於妾祖姑，無妾祖姑，則易牲而祔於女君可也。

translations.literal: Examining the Record: 'A concubine is enshrined with her husband's concubine-grandmother; if there is no concubine-grandmother, then change the victim and enshrine with the primary wife— this is permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Examining the Record: 'A concubine is enshrined with her husband's concubine-grandmother; if there is no concubine-grandmother, then change the victim and enshrine with the primary wife—this is permitted.

sentences.zh: 』始章太后於昭太后，論昭穆而言，則非妾祖姑，又非女君，於義不當。

translations.literal: ' At the outset Empress Dowager Zhang toward Empress Dowager Zhao— speaking of zhao and mu— she is neither concubine-grandmother nor primary wife; by principle this is not appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset Empress Dowager Zhang toward Empress Dowager Zhao—speaking of zhao and mu—she is neither concubine-grandmother nor primary wife; by principle this is not appropriate.

sentences.zh: 伏尋昭太后名位允極，昔初祔之始，自上祔於趙后，即安于西廟，並皆幣告諸室。

translations.literal: Examining further: Empress Dowager Zhao's name and rank reached the utmost; when first enshrined, from above she was enshrined with Empress Dowager Zhao and settled in the western temple— both received silk announcement to all chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Examining further: Empress Dowager Zhao's name and rank reached the utmost; when first enshrined, from above she was enshrined with Empress Dowager Zhao and settled in the western temple—both received silk announcement to all chambers.

sentences.zh: 古者大事必告，又云每事必告。

translations.literal: In antiquity great affairs must be announced; it also says every affair must be announced.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity great affairs had to be announced; it also says that every affair must be announced.

sentences.zh: 禮，牲幣雜用。

translations.literal: By ritual, victims and silk are used mixed.
translations.idiomatic: By ritual, victims and silk offerings are used together.

sentences.zh: 檢魏、晉以來，互有不同。

translations.literal: Examining Wei and Jin onward, they differ from each other.
translations.idiomatic: Examining Wei and Jin onward, practice differs from case to case.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十六年，下禮官辨正。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Yuanjia, order the ritual officers to distinguish and correct.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Yuanjia, the court ordered the ritual officers to distinguish and correct the practice.

sentences.zh: 太學博士殷靈祚議稱：『吉事用牲，凶事用幣。

translations.literal: Erudite Yin Lingzuo of the Imperial Academy argued: 'Auspicious affairs use victims; inauspicious affairs use silk.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Yin Lingzuo of the Imperial Academy argued: 'For auspicious affairs one uses victims; for inauspicious affairs one uses silk.

sentences.zh: 』自茲而後，吉凶為判，已是一代之成典。

translations.literal: ' From then onward auspicious and inauspicious were distinguished— already a canon of the age.
translations.idiomatic: From then onward auspicious and inauspicious were distinguished—already a canon of the age.

sentences.zh: 今事雖不全凶，亦未近吉，故宜依舊，以幣徧告二廟。

translations.literal: Now the affair, though not wholly inauspicious, is also not near auspicious— therefore should follow the former practice and announce with silk to both temples throughout.
translations.idiomatic: Now the affair, though not wholly inauspicious, is also not near auspicious—therefore should follow the former practice and announce with silk to both temples throughout.

sentences.zh: 又尋昭太后毀主，無義陳列於太祖，博士欲依虞主埋於廟兩階之間。

translations.literal: Also examining the destroyed tablet of Empress Dowager Zhao— there is no principle for displaying it before the Grand Ancestor; the erudites wish to follow the provisional tablet and bury it between the steps of the temple.
translations.idiomatic: Also examining the destroyed tablet of Empress Dowager Zhao—there is no principle for displaying it before the Grand Ancestor; the erudites wish to follow the provisional tablet and bury it between the steps of the temple.

sentences.zh: 按階間本以埋告幣埋虞主之所。

translations.literal: Examining further: the space between the steps was originally for burying announcement silk and the provisional tablet.
translations.idiomatic: Examining further: the space between the steps was originally for burying announcement silk and the provisional spirit tablet.

sentences.zh: 昔虞喜云，依五經典議，以毀主祔於虞主，埋於廟之北牆，最為可據。

translations.literal: Formerly Yu Xi said: following the deliberations of the Five Classics, enshrining the destroyed tablet with the provisional tablet and burying it at the temple's north wall is most authoritative.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Yu Xi said: following the deliberations of the Five Classics, enshrining the destroyed tablet with the provisional tablet and burying it at the temple's north wall is the most authoritative practice.

sentences.zh: 昭太后神主毀之埋之後，上室不可不虛置，太后便應上下升之。

translations.literal: After the spirit tablet of Empress Dowager Zhao is destroyed and buried, the upper chamber cannot remain empty— Empress Dowager Xuan should ascend to fill it.
translations.idiomatic: After the spirit tablet of Empress Dowager Zhao is destroyed and buried, the upper chamber cannot remain empty—Empress Dowager Xuan should ascend to fill it.

sentences.zh: 既升之頃，又應設脯醢以安神。

translations.literal: At the moment of ascent dried meat and pickled offerings should also be set to settle the spirit.
translations.idiomatic: At the moment of ascent, dried meat and pickled offerings should also be set out to settle the spirit.

sentences.zh: 今禮官所議，謬略未周。

translations.literal: Now the ritual officers' deliberation is erroneous and incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: Now the ritual officers' deliberation is mistaken and incomplete.

sentences.zh: 遷毀事大，請廣詳訪。

translations.literal: Relocation and destruction are great affairs— please investigate broadly in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Relocation and destruction are great affairs—please investigate broadly in detail.

sentences.zh: 」左僕射劉秉等七人同匪子。

translations.literal: " Left Vice Director Liu Bing and seven others agreed with Feizi.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Liu Bing and seven others agreed with Feizi.

sentences.zh: 左丞王諶重參議，謂：「以幣徧告二廟，埋毀殷主於北牆。

translations.literal: Left Assistant Director Wang Chen reviewed the deliberation, stating: "Announce with silk to both temples throughout; bury the destroyed yin tablet at the north wall.
translations.idiomatic: Left Assistant Director Wang Chen reviewed the deliberation, stating: "Announce with silk to both temples throughout, and bury the destroyed yin tablet at the north wall.

sentences.zh: 宣太后上室，仍設脯醢以安神，匪子議為允。

translations.literal: At Empress Dowager Xuan's upper chamber, still set dried meat and pickled offerings to settle the spirit— Feizi's deliberation is acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: At Empress Dowager Xuan's upper chamber, still set dried meat and pickled offerings to settle the spirit—Feizi's deliberation is acceptable.

translations.idiomatic: An edict approved it.

translations.literal: In the third year of Taihe under Emperor Ming of Wei, an edict stated: "By ritual, when the queen has no heir, a collateral son is chosen to continue the great line— then one should inherit the orthodox line and uphold public principle; how can one consider private kin?
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taihe under Emperor Ming of Wei, an edict stated: "By ritual, when the queen has no heir, a collateral son is chosen to continue the great line—then one should inherit the orthodox line and uphold public principle; how can one consider private kin?

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan of Han succeeded Emperor Zhao and later added the posthumous title of Emperor for his father the Duke of Ding;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan of Han succeeded Emperor Zhao and later added the posthumous imperial title for his father the Duke of Ding;

sentences.zh: 哀帝以外蕃援立，而董宏等稱引亡秦，或誤朝議，遂尊恭皇，立廟京師，又寵蕃妾，使比長信，僭差無禮，人神弗佑，非罪師丹忠正之諫，用致丁、傅焚如之禍。

translations.literal: Emperor Ai, installed from an outer fief, and Dong Hong and others cited the fallen Qin— some misleading court deliberation— then honored the Respectful Emperor, established a temple in the capital, and favored a fief concubine equaling Changxin— excessive breach of ritual; neither human nor spirit blessed them; had it not been for Shi Dan's loyal and upright remonstrance, the disaster of Ding and Fu burning like tinder would have resulted.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ai, installed from an outer fief, and Dong Hong and others cited the fallen Qin—some misleading court deliberation—then honored the Respectful Emperor, established a temple in the capital, and favored a fief concubine equaling Changxin—excessive breach of ritual; neither human nor spirit blessed them; had it not been for Shi Dan's loyal and upright remonstrance, the disaster of Ding and Fu burning like tinder would have resulted.

sentences.zh: 自是之後，相踵行之。

translations.literal: From then onward this was practiced in succession.
translations.idiomatic: From then onward this practice was followed in succession.

sentences.zh: 其令公卿有司，深以前代為誡。

translations.literal: Order the dukes, ministers, and responsible officials to take deeply as warning the former generations.
translations.idiomatic: Order the dukes, ministers, and responsible officials to take the former generations deeply as a warning.

sentences.zh: 後嗣萬一有由諸侯入奉大統，則當明為人後之義。

translations.literal: If hereafter a successor by any chance enters from among the feudal lords to receive the great succession, then the meaning of becoming another's heir should be made clear.
translations.idiomatic: If hereafter a successor should by any chance enter from among the feudal lords to receive the great succession, then the meaning of becoming another's heir should be made clear.

sentences.zh: 敢為佞邪，導諛君上，妄建非正之號，謂考為皇，稱妣為后，則股肱大臣，誅之無赦。

translations.literal: Whoever dares flatter and deceive the lord above, rashly establishing non-orthodox titles— calling father Emperor and mother Empress— the great ministers as arms and legs shall execute without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever dares flatter and deceive the lord above, rashly establishing non-orthodox titles—calling father Emperor and mother Empress—the great ministers as arms and legs shall execute without pardon.

sentences.zh: 其書之金策，藏之宗廟，著于令典。

translations.literal: Inscribe this on the golden covenant; store it in the ancestral temple; record it in the established canon.
translations.idiomatic: Inscribe this on the golden covenant, store it in the ancestral temple, and record it in the established canon.

translations.literal: " Thereafter when Gaogui and Changdao were installed, none honored outer kin.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter when Gaogui and Changdao were installed, none honored outer kin.

sentences.zh: 晉愍帝建興四年，司徒梁芬議追尊之禮，帝既不從，而左僕射索綝等亦稱引魏制，以為不可。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianxing under Emperor Min of Jin, Director of the Masters of Ceremony Liang Fen deliberated on the ritual of posthumous honor— the emperor did not follow; Left Vice Director Suo Lin and others also cited Wei regulations as grounds that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jianxing under Emperor Min of Jin, Director of the Masters of Ceremony Liang Fen deliberated on the ritual of posthumous honor—the emperor did not follow; Left Vice Director Suo Lin and others also cited Wei regulations as grounds that it could not be done.

sentences.zh: 故追贈吳王為太保而已。

translations.literal: Therefore Prince Wu of Wu was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Tutor only.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Prince Wu of Wu was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Tutor and nothing more.

sentences.zh: 元帝太興二年，有司言琅邪恭王宜稱皇考。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taixing under Emperor Yuan, the responsible officials stated that Prince Gong of Langye should be called Imperial Father.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taixing under Emperor Yuan, the responsible officials stated that Prince Gong of Langye should be styled Imperial Father.

sentences.zh: 賀循議云：「禮典之義，子不敢以己爵加其父號。

translations.literal: He Xun deliberated: "The meaning of ritual canon— a son dares not add his own rank to his father's title.
translations.idiomatic: He Xun deliberated: "The meaning of ritual canon—a son dares not add his own rank to his father's title.

sentences.zh: 」帝又從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor again followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again followed this.

sentences.zh: 二漢此典棄矣。

translations.literal: This canon of the two Han dynasties was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: This canon of the two Han dynasties was abandoned thereafter.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝有愛女曰淑涉，三月而夭，帝痛之甚，追封諡為平原懿公主，葬於南陵，立廟京師。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Wei had a beloved daughter named Shushe; she died at three months; the emperor grieved deeply; posthumously enfeoffed and titled her Princess Yi of Pingyuan; buried at Nanling; established a temple in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Wei had a beloved daughter named Shushe; she died at three months; the emperor grieved deeply; he posthumously enfeoffed and titled her Princess Yi of Pingyuan, buried her at Nanling, and established a temple in the capital.

sentences.zh: 無前典，非禮也。

translations.literal: There was no prior canon— not ritual.
translations.idiomatic: There was no prior canon—not ritual.

sentences.zh: 宋孝武帝孝建元年七月辛酉，有司奏：「東平沖王年稚無後，唯殤服五月。

translations.literal: On the xinyou day of the seventh month of the first year of Xiaojian under Emperor Xiaowu of Song, the responsible officials memorialized: "Prince Chong of Dongping was young and without heir; only infant-spirit mourning garments for five months.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinyou day of the seventh month in the first year of Xiaojian under Emperor Xiaowu of Song, the responsible officials memorialized: "Prince Chong of Dongping was young and without heir; only infant-spirit mourning garments for five months.

sentences.zh: 雖臣不殤君，應有主祭，而國是追贈，又無其臣。

translations.literal: Although a minister does not mourn for his lord in infant-spirit rites, there should be a chief sacrificer; yet the state was posthumously enfeoffed and has no ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Although a minister does not mourn for his lord in infant-spirit rites, there should be a chief sacrificer; yet the state was posthumously enfeoffed and had no ministers.

translations.literal: It is unclear whether to destroy the spirit tablet and establish a temple— should enshrinement elsewhere be made or not?
translations.idiomatic: It is unclear whether to destroy the spirit tablet and establish a temple—should enshrinement elsewhere be made or not?

translations.literal: Refer to the ritual officers for detailed deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Refer the matter to the ritual officers for detailed deliberation.

translations.literal: " Erudite Xu Hong of the Imperial Academy argued: "The prince having no heir and posthumous enfeoffment having no ministers— when infant-spirit mourning garments are complete the spirit tablet should be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Xu Hong of the Imperial Academy argued: "The prince having no heir and posthumous enfeoffment having no ministers—when infant-spirit mourning garments are complete the spirit tablet should be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 記曰：『殤與無後者，從祖祔食。

translations.literal: The Record says: 'Infant spirits and those without posterity follow the ancestor in enshrinement and sharing food.
translations.idiomatic: The Record says: 'Infant spirits and those without posterity follow the ancestor in enshrinement and shared offerings.

sentences.zh: 』又曰：『士大夫不得祔於諸侯，祔於祖之為士大夫者。

translations.literal: ' It also says: 'Grand officers cannot be enshrined with feudal lords; enshrine with the ancestor who was a grand officer.
translations.idiomatic: It also says: 'Grand officers cannot be enshrined with feudal lords; enshrine with the ancestor who was a grand officer.

translations.literal: ' Examining further: feudal lords cannot be enshrined with the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Examining further: feudal lords cannot be enshrined with the Son of Heaven.

translations.idiomatic: Prince Chong should be enshrined in the temple of an ancestor who was a king—in this case, the temple of Prince Jing of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: " An edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 』注稱：『緣為慈母後之義，父妾無子，亦可命己庶子為之後也。

sentences.zh: 』考尋斯義，父母妾之祭，不必唯子。

translations.literal: ' Examining this meaning— sacrifice to the father's and mother's concubines need not be only by the son.
translations.idiomatic: Examining this meaning—sacrifice to the father's and mother's concubines need not be only by the son.

translations.literal: Prince Xuan of Jiangxia was the Heir Apparent in person— lineage from the chief minister; a branch of the imperial kin; meeting untimely misfortune; the sage sovereign pitied and mourned; lowered from imperial favor; succeeded to continue the emblematic line; opened the great fief; the state became ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xuan of Jiangxia was the Heir Apparent in person—lineage from the chief minister; a branch of the imperial kin; meeting untimely misfortune; the sage sovereign pitied and mourned; lowered from imperial favor; succeeded to continue the emblematic line; opened the great fief; the state became ancestor.

sentences.zh: 始王夫人載育明懿，則一國之正，上無所厭，哀敬得申。

translations.literal: The first prince's lady bore and nurtured with bright virtue— then she was orthodox mother of the state; above there was nothing to diminish; grief and reverence could be expressed.
translations.idiomatic: The first prince's lady bore and nurtured with bright virtue—then she was orthodox mother of the state; above there was nothing to diminish; grief and reverence could be expressed.

sentences.zh: 祭之日，誰為主？

translations.literal: On the day of sacrifice, who should be chief?
translations.idiomatic: On the day of sacrifice, who should serve as chief sacrificer?

translations.idiomatic: Concurrent Director of Ceremonies Yu Weizhi argued: "Three days after burial the state ministers follow provisional regulations and remove mourning garments.

sentences.zh: 而靈筵猶存，朔望及朞忌，諸臣宜還臨哭，變服衣𢂿，使上卿主祭。

translations.idiomatic: Yet the spirit mats remain; on new and full moon and periodic anniversaries the ministers should return to attend and weep, changing into fine hemp mourning dress, with a senior minister serving as chief sacrificer.

sentences.zh: 王既未有後，又無三年服者，朞親服除，而國尚存，便宜立廟，為國之始祖。

translations.literal: The prince having no heir yet and no one in three-year mourning— when mourning of close kin ends yet the state still exists, it is appropriate to establish a temple as the state's founding ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: The prince having no heir yet and no one in three-year mourning—when mourning of close kin ends yet the state still exists, it is appropriate to establish a temple as the state's founding ancestor.

sentences.zh: 服除之日，神主暫祔食祖廟。

translations.literal: On the day mourning garments are removed the spirit tablet should temporarily be enshrined to share food at the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: On the day mourning garments are removed, the spirit tablet should temporarily be enshrined to share food at the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 諸王不得祖天子，宜祔從祖國廟，還居新廟之室。

translations.literal: Princes cannot take the Son of Heaven as ancestor— should enshrine at the collateral state temple; then return to the new temple's chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Princes cannot take the Son of Heaven as ancestor—should enshrine at the collateral state temple; then return to the new temple's chamber.

sentences.zh: 未有嗣之前，四時饗薦，常使上卿主之。

translations.literal: Before an heir exists, the four seasonal offerings and feasts should regularly have a senior minister preside.
translations.idiomatic: Before an heir exists, the four seasonal offerings and feasts should regularly be presided over by a senior minister.

translations.idiomatic: Erudite Yu He of the Imperial Academy argued: "The Court Etiquette states: 'The Son of Heaven has an empress and has ladies.

translations.idiomatic: Tann Gong states: 'Shun was buried at Cangwu; the three consorts did not follow.

translations.literal: ' The Meaning of Marriage states: 'The empress establishes the six palaces, with three ladies.
translations.idiomatic: The Meaning of Marriage states: 'The empress establishes the six palaces, with three ladies.

sentences.zh: 』然則三妃即三夫人也。

translations.literal: ' Thus the three consorts are the three ladies.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the three consorts are the three ladies.

sentences.zh: 后之有三妃，猶天子之有三公也。

translations.literal: The empress having three consorts is like the Son of Heaven having three excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: The empress having three consorts is analogous to the Son of Heaven having three excellencies.

sentences.zh: 按周禮，三公八命，諸侯七命。

translations.literal: Examining the Rites of Zhou, the three excellencies receive eight commands; feudal lords receive seven commands.
translations.idiomatic: Examining the Rites of Zhou, the three excellencies receive eight commands, while feudal lords receive seven commands.

sentences.zh: 三公既尊於列國諸侯，三妃亦貴於庶邦夫人。

translations.literal: The three excellencies being exalted above the feudal lords of the ranks— the three consorts are also honored above the ladies of other states.
translations.idiomatic: The three excellencies being exalted above the feudal lords of the ranks—the three consorts are also honored above the ladies of other states.

sentences.zh: 據春秋傳，仲子非魯惠元嫡，尚得考彼別宮。

translations.literal: Examining the Spring and Autumn Commentary, Zhongzi was not the primary wife of Duke Hui of Lu, yet could be sacrificed to in a separate palace.
translations.idiomatic: Examining the Spring and Autumn Commentary, Zhongzi was not the primary wife of Duke Hui of Lu, yet could still be sacrificed to in a separate palace.

sentences.zh: 今貴妃是秩，天之崇班，理應立此新廟。

translations.idiomatic: It remains unclear when enshrinement of the Honored Consort in the temple should occur.

translations.idiomatic: On the day of entering the temple—should there first be enshrinement, or merely entering the new temple?

translations.idiomatic: If entering the temple during daxing or chan, may sacrifice be performed when the four seasons arrive?

translations.idiomatic: May Prince Xin'an, while still under heart-mourning regulations, personally perform sacrifice?

translations.idiomatic: Chang is the name of an auspicious sacrifice—during daxing and chan one may not yet enter the temple; it should be after chan mourning ends.

translations.idiomatic: Moreover after zucu there is all the more no grounds for enshrinement.

translations.literal: If the temple is not yet established— at what place should sacrifice be performed?
translations.idiomatic: If the temple is not yet established—at what place should sacrifice be performed?

sentences.zh: 」游擊將軍徐爰議以為：「國無後，於制除罷。

translations.literal: " General of Guerrilla Forces Xu Ai argued: "A state without heir— by regulation mourning ends and the affair ceases.
translations.idiomatic: General of Guerrilla Forces Xu Ai argued: "A state without heir—by regulation mourning ends and the affair ceases.

sentences.zh: 始封之君，宜存繼嗣。

translations.literal: The prince first enfeoffed should preserve continuing succession.
translations.idiomatic: The prince first enfeoffed should preserve the continuing line of succession.

sentences.zh: 皇子追贈，則為始祖。

translations.literal: A prince posthumously enfeoffed becomes the founding ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: A prince posthumously enfeoffed becomes the founding ancestor of the line.

sentences.zh: 臣不殤君，事著前準，豈容虛闕烝嘗，以俟有後。

translations.literal: A minister does not mourn for his lord in infant-spirit rites— matter clear in prior standards— how can zheng and chang sacrifice be vainly omitted while awaiting an heir?
translations.idiomatic: A minister does not mourn for his lord in infant-spirit rites—matter clear in prior standards—how can zheng and chang sacrifice be vainly omitted while awaiting an heir?

sentences.zh: 謂宜立廟作主，三卿主祭依舊。

translations.literal: I hold that a temple should be established and the tablet made; the Three Excellencies should preside over sacrifice as before.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that a temple should be established and the tablet made, and that the Three Excellencies should preside over sacrifice as before.

sentences.zh: 」通關博議，以爰議為允。

translations.literal: " Upon broad deliberation through all gates Ai's view was held acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Upon broad deliberation through all gates Ai's view was held acceptable.

sentences.zh: 令便立廟。

translations.literal: An order immediately established the temple.
translations.idiomatic: An edict immediately ordered the temple established.

sentences.zh: 廟成作主，依晉陵王近例，先暫祔廬陵孝獻王廟。

translations.literal: When the temple was complete the tablet was made; following the recent precedent of the Prince of Jinling, first temporarily enshrined at Prince Xian of Luling's temple.
translations.idiomatic: When the temple was complete the tablet was made; following the recent precedent of the Prince of Jinling, it was first temporarily enshrined at Prince Xian of Luling's temple.

sentences.zh: 祭竟，神主即還新廟。

translations.literal: When sacrifice was complete the spirit tablet immediately returned to the new temple.
translations.idiomatic: When sacrifice was complete, the spirit tablet immediately returned to the new temple.

sentences.zh: 未立後之前，常使國上卿主祭。

translations.literal: Before an heir was established, regularly have the state's senior minister preside over sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Before an heir was established, the state's senior minister should regularly preside over sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 禮云：「共工氏之霸九州，其子句龍曰后土，能平九土，故祀以為社。

translations.literal: The Rites state: "When Gong Gong dominated the nine provinces, his son Gou Long was called Lord of Earth; he could level the nine lands— therefore he was sacrificed to as the altar of Earth.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites state: "When Gong Gong dominated the nine provinces, his son Gou Long was called Lord of Earth; he could level the nine lands—therefore he was sacrificed to as the altar of Earth.

sentences.zh: 」周以甲日祭之，用日之始也。

translations.literal: " Zhou sacrificed on the jia day— using the beginning of the day.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou sacrificed on the jia day—using the beginning of the day.

sentences.zh: 「社所以神地之道。

translations.literal: "The altar of Earth is how one spiritualizes the way of earth.
translations.idiomatic: The altar of Earth is how one spiritualizes the way of earth.

sentences.zh: 地載萬物，天垂象。

translations.literal: Earth carries the myriad things; Heaven displays the signs.
translations.idiomatic: Earth carries the myriad things, and Heaven displays the signs.

sentences.zh: 取財於地，取法於天。

translations.literal: Take wealth from earth; take law from heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Take wealth from earth and law from heaven.

sentences.zh: 是以尊天而親地。

translations.literal: Therefore revere heaven and be close to earth.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore one reveres heaven and draws close to earth.

sentences.zh: 故教民美報焉。

translations.literal: Thus the people are taught beautiful recompense.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the people are taught to make beautiful recompense.

sentences.zh: 家主中霤而國主社，示本也。

translations.literal: The household takes the central rafter as lord; the state takes the altar of Earth as lord— showing the root.
translations.idiomatic: The household takes the central rafter as lord; the state takes the altar of Earth as lord—showing the root.

sentences.zh: 」故言報本反始。

translations.literal: " Therefore it speaks of recompensing the root and returning to the beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore it speaks of recompensing the root and returning to the beginning.

sentences.zh: 烈山氏之有天下，其子曰農，能殖百穀。

translations.literal: When the Flame Emperor possessed the realm, his son was called Nong and could propagate the hundred grains.
translations.idiomatic: When the Flame Emperor possessed the realm, his son was called Nong and could propagate the hundred kinds of grain.

sentences.zh: 其裔曰柱，佐顓頊為稷官，主農事，周棄係之，法施於人，故祀以為稷。

translations.literal: His descendant was called Zhu; he assisted Zhuanxu as officer of grain, presiding over agricultural affairs; Zhou's Hou Ji succeeded him; his method benefited the people— therefore he was sacrificed to as the god of grain.
translations.idiomatic: His descendant was called Zhu; he assisted Zhuanxu as officer of grain, presiding over agricultural affairs; Zhou's Hou Ji succeeded him; his method benefited the people—therefore he was sacrificed to as the god of grain.

sentences.zh: 禮：「王為羣姓立社曰太社，王自為立社曰王社。

translations.literal: The Rites: "The king establishes an altar of Earth for the clans— called the Grand Altar of Earth; the king establishes an altar of Earth for himself— called the King's Altar of Earth.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites: "The king establishes an altar of Earth for the clans—called the Grand Altar of Earth; the king establishes an altar of Earth for himself—called the King's Altar of Earth.

sentences.zh: 」故國有二社，而稷亦有二也。

translations.literal: " Therefore the state has two altars of Earth, and the god of grain also has two.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the state has two altars of Earth, and the god of grain also has two.

sentences.zh: 漢、魏則有官社，無稷，故常二社一稷也。

translations.literal: Han and Wei had the official altar of Earth but no god of grain— therefore regularly two altars of Earth and one god of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Han and Wei had the official altar of Earth but no god of grain—therefore regularly two altars of Earth and one god of grain.

sentences.zh: 晉初仍魏，無所增損。

translations.literal: Early Jin followed Wei without increase or decrease.
translations.idiomatic: Early Jin followed Wei without adding or subtracting anything.

sentences.zh: 至太康九年，改建宗廟，而社稷壇與廟俱徙。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Taikang the ancestral temple was rebuilt; the altars of soil and grain were moved together with the temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Taikang the ancestral temple was rebuilt, and the altars of soil and grain were moved together with it.

sentences.zh: 乃詔曰：「社實一神，其并二社之祀。

translations.literal: An edict then stated: "The altar of Earth is truly one spirit— combine the sacrifice of the two altars of Earth.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then stated: "The altar of Earth is truly one spirit—combine the sacrifice of the two altars of Earth.

sentences.zh: 」於是車騎司馬傅咸表曰：「祭法二社各有其義。

translations.literal: " Thereupon General of Chariots and Cavalry Fu Xian submitted a memorial: "The Record of Sacrifice— the two altars of Earth each have their meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon General of Chariots and Cavalry Fu Xian submitted a memorial: "The Record of Sacrifice—the two altars of Earth each have their meaning.

sentences.zh: 天子尊事郊廟，故冕而躬耕。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven reverently serves the suburban altars and temples— therefore wears the sacrificial cap and personally plows.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven reverently serves the suburban altars and temples—therefore wears the sacrificial cap and personally plows.

sentences.zh: 躬耕也者，所以重孝享之粢盛，致殷薦於上帝也。

translations.literal: Personal plowing is to emphasize the sacrificial grain of filial offerings— rendering the yin offering to the Lord on High.
translations.idiomatic: Personal plowing is to emphasize the sacrificial grain of filial offerings—rendering the yin offering to the Lord on High.

sentences.zh: 穀梁傳曰：『天子親耕以供粢盛。

translations.literal: The Guliang Commentary says: 'The Son of Heaven personally plows to supply the sacrificial grain.
translations.idiomatic: The Guliang Commentary says: 'The Son of Heaven personally plows in order to supply the sacrificial grain.

sentences.zh: 』親耕，謂自報，自為立社者，為籍而報也。

translations.literal: ' Personal plowing means self-recompense; establishing an altar for oneself— for the field and recompense.
translations.idiomatic: Personal plowing means self-recompense; establishing an altar for oneself—for the field and recompense.

sentences.zh: 國以人為本，人以穀為命，故又為百姓立社而祈報焉。

translations.literal: The state takes the people as foundation; people take grain as life— therefore also establish an altar of Earth for the hundred surnames and pray for recompense.
translations.idiomatic: The state takes the people as foundation; people take grain as life—therefore also establish an altar of Earth for the hundred surnames and pray for recompense.

sentences.zh: 事異報殊，此社之所以有二也。

translations.literal: The affair differs and recompense differs— this is why there are two altars of Earth.
translations.idiomatic: The affair differs and recompense differs—this is why there are two altars of Earth.

sentences.zh: 王景侯之論王社，亦謂春祈籍田，秋而報之也。

translations.literal: Wang Jinghou's discussion of the King's Altar of Earth also says spring prayer at the field of sacrifice, autumn recompense.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jinghou's discussion of the King's Altar of Earth also speaks of spring prayer at the field of sacrifice and autumn recompense.

sentences.zh: 其論太社，則曰『王者布下圻內，為百姓立之，謂之太社，不自立之於京師也』。

translations.literal: His discussion of the Grand Altar of Earth says: 'The king spreads within the inner domain; establishes it for the hundred surnames— called the Grand Altar of Earth; does not establish it for himself in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: His discussion of the Grand Altar of Earth says: 'The king spreads within the inner domain; establishes it for the hundred surnames—called the Grand Altar of Earth; does not establish it for himself in the capital.

sentences.zh: 景侯此論，據祭法『大夫以下，成羣立社，曰置社』。

translations.literal: Jinghou's discussion cites the Record of Sacrifice: 'Grand officers and below— when a group is formed establish an altar of Earth— called establishing an altar.
translations.idiomatic: Jinghou's discussion cites the Record of Sacrifice: 'Grand officers and below—when a group is formed establish an altar of Earth—called establishing an altar.

sentences.zh: 景侯解曰：『今之里社是也。

translations.literal: Jinghou explains: 'The present neighborhood altar of Earth is such.
translations.idiomatic: Jinghou explains: 'The present neighborhood altar of Earth is of this kind.

sentences.zh: 』景侯解祭法，則以置社為人間之社矣。

translations.literal: Jinghou explaining the Record of Sacrifice takes establishing an altar as the people's altar of Earth.
translations.idiomatic: In Jinghou's explanation of the Record of Sacrifice, establishing an altar is taken as the people's altar of Earth.

sentences.zh: 而別論復以太社為人間之社，未曉此旨也。

translations.literal: Yet separately discussing takes the Grand Altar of Earth as the people's altar— the intent of this is not understood.
translations.idiomatic: Yet separately discussing takes the Grand Altar of Earth as the people's altar—the intent of this is not understood.

sentences.zh: 太社，天子為民而祀，故稱天子社。

translations.literal: The Grand Altar of Earth— the Son of Heaven sacrifices for the people— therefore called the Son of Heaven's altar of Earth.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Altar of Earth—the Son of Heaven sacrifices for the people—therefore called the Son of Heaven's altar of Earth.

sentences.zh: 郊特牲曰：『天子太社，必受霜露風雨。

translations.literal: Suburban Sacrifice states: 'The Son of Heaven's Grand Altar of Earth must receive frost, dew, wind, and rain.
translations.idiomatic: Suburban Sacrifice states: 'The Son of Heaven's Grand Altar of Earth must be exposed to frost, dew, wind, and rain.

sentences.zh: 』夫以羣姓之眾，王者通為立社，故稱太社。

translations.literal: For the multitude of the clans the king universally establishes altars of Earth— therefore called Grand Altar of Earth.
translations.idiomatic: For the multitude of the clans the king universally establishes altars of Earth—therefore called Grand Altar of Earth.

sentences.zh: 若夫置社，其數不一，蓋以里所為名。

translations.literal: As for establishing altars, their number is not one— generally named by the neighborhood.
translations.idiomatic: As for establishing altars, their number is not one—generally named by the neighborhood.

sentences.zh: 左氏傳盟于清丘之社是也。

translations.literal: The Zuo Commentary's covenant at Qingqiu's altar of Earth is such.
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Commentary's account of the covenant at Qingqiu's altar of Earth is such.

sentences.zh: 人間之社，既已不稱太矣。

translations.literal: The people's altar of Earth— already not called Grand.
translations.idiomatic: The people's altar of Earth—already not called Grand.

sentences.zh: 若復不立之京都，當安所立乎？

translations.literal: If again not established in the capital— where should it be established?
translations.idiomatic: If again not established in the capital—where should it be established?

sentences.zh: 祭法又曰：『王為羣姓立七祀。

translations.literal: The Record of Sacrifice also says: 'The king establishes seven sacrifices for the clans.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Sacrifice also says: 'The king establishes seven sacrifices on behalf of the clans.

sentences.zh: 自為立七祀。

translations.literal: Establishes seven sacrifices for himself.
translations.idiomatic: He also establishes seven sacrifices for himself.

sentences.zh: 』言自為者，自為而祀也。

translations.literal: Speaking of "for himself"— sacrifice for oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Speaking of "for himself"—sacrifice for oneself.

sentences.zh: 為羣姓者，為羣姓而祀也。

translations.literal: For the clans— sacrifice for the clans.
translations.idiomatic: For the clans—sacrifice for the clans.

sentences.zh: 太社與七祀，其文正等。

translations.literal: The Grand Altar of Earth and the seven sacrifices— their texts are equally ranked.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Altar of Earth and the seven sacrifices—their texts are equally ranked.

sentences.zh: 說者窮此，因云墳籍但有五祀無七祀也。

translations.literal: Expositors exhaust this and therefore say the canonical texts have only five sacrifices, not seven.
translations.idiomatic: Expositors exhaust this point and therefore say the canonical texts have only five sacrifices, not seven.

sentences.zh: 按祭五祀，國之大祀，七者小祀。

translations.literal: Examining sacrifice to the five sacrifices— great sacrifice of the state; the seven are lesser sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Examining sacrifice to the five sacrifices—great sacrifice of the state; the seven are lesser sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 周禮所云祭凡小祀，則墨冕之屬也。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou speaks of sacrificing all lesser sacrifices— then black sacrificial cap and the like.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou speaks of sacrificing all lesser sacrifices—then black sacrificial cap and the like.

sentences.zh: 景侯解大厲曰：『如周杜伯，鬼有所歸，乃不為厲。

translations.literal: Jinghou explaining great pestilence says: 'Like Zhou's Duke of Du— when the ghost has a place to return, then it does not become a pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: Jinghou explaining great pestilence says: 'Like Zhou's Duke of Du—when the ghost has a place to return, then it does not become a pestilence.

sentences.zh: 』今云無二社者，稱景侯祭法不謂無二，則曰口傳無其文也。

translations.literal: Now saying there are not two altars of Earth— citing Jinghou's Record of Sacrifice does not mean there are not two; it says oral tradition has no text.
translations.idiomatic: Now saying there are not two altars of Earth—citing Jinghou's Record of Sacrifice does not mean there are not two; it says oral tradition has no text.

sentences.zh: 夫以景侯之明，擬議而後為解，而欲以口論除明文。

translations.literal: Given Jinghou's clarity— deliberating before making explanation— yet wishing to remove explicit text by oral argument.
translations.idiomatic: Given Jinghou's clarity—deliberating before making explanation—yet wishing to remove explicit text by oral argument.

sentences.zh: 如此，非但二社，當是思惟景侯之後解，亦未易除也。

translations.literal: Thus not only the two altars of Earth— one should reflect on Jinghou's later explanations; they too are not easily removed.
translations.idiomatic: Thus not only the two altars of Earth—one should reflect on Jinghou's later explanations; they too are not easily removed.

sentences.zh: 前被敕，尚書召誥：『社于新邑，唯一太牢，』不立二社之明義也。

translations.literal: Formerly receiving the edict— the Announcement of the Prince of Shao: 'Altar of Earth at the new city— only one Grand Victim'— the clear meaning of not establishing two altars of Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly receiving the edict—the Announcement of the Prince of Shao: 'Altar of Earth at the new city—only one Grand Victim'—the clear meaning of not establishing two altars of Earth.

sentences.zh: 按郊特牲曰：『社稷太牢。

translations.literal: Examining Suburban Sacrifice: 'Altars of soil and grain— Grand Victim.
translations.idiomatic: Examining Suburban Sacrifice: 'Altars of soil and grain—Grand Victim.

sentences.zh: 』必援一牢之文，以明社之無二，則稷無牲矣。

translations.literal: Must cite the text of one victim to show the altar of Earth has not two— then the god of grain has no victim.
translations.idiomatic: Must cite the text of one victim to show the altar of Earth has not two—then the god of grain has no victim.

sentences.zh: 說者則曰，舉社以明稷。

translations.literal: Expositors then say: cite the altar of Earth to clarify the god of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Expositors then say: one cites the altar of Earth in order to clarify the god of grain.

sentences.zh: 苟可舉社以明稷，何獨不可舉一以明二。

translations.literal: If one may cite the altar of Earth to clarify the god of grain— why alone may one not cite one to clarify two?
translations.idiomatic: If one may cite the altar of Earth to clarify the god of grain—why alone may one not cite one to clarify two?

sentences.zh: 『國之大事，在祀與戎』。

translations.literal: "The great affairs of a state lie in sacrifice and war."
translations.idiomatic: "The great affairs of a state are sacrifice and war."

sentences.zh: 若有過而除之，不若過而存之。

translations.literal: If there is excess and one removes it— better excess and preserve it.
translations.idiomatic: If there is excess and one removes it—better excess and preserve it.

sentences.zh: 況存之有義，而除之無據乎。

translations.literal: How much more when preservation has principle and removal lacks evidence?
translations.idiomatic: How much more so when preservation has principle and removal lacks evidence?

sentences.zh: 周禮封人『掌設社壝』。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou Border Officer 'presides over setting up the altar platform of Earth.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou, Border Officer, states: 'He presides over setting up the altar platform of Earth.

sentences.zh: 無稷字。

translations.literal: There is no character for god of grain.
translations.idiomatic: There is no character for the god of grain.

sentences.zh: 今帝社無稷，蓋出於此。

translations.literal: Now the imperial altar of Earth has no god of grain— probably arising from this.
translations.idiomatic: Now the imperial altar of Earth has no god of grain—probably arising from this.

sentences.zh: 然國主社稷，故經傳動稱社稷。

translations.literal: Yet the state takes lordship of the altars of soil and grain— therefore classics and commentaries often say altars of soil and grain together.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the state takes lordship of the altars of soil and grain—therefore classics and commentaries often say altars of soil and grain together.

sentences.zh: 周禮，王祭稷則絺冕。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou: when the king sacrifices to the god of grain he wears the xi sacrificial cap.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou: when the king sacrifices to the god of grain, he wears the xi sacrificial cap.

sentences.zh: 此王社有稷之文也。

translations.literal: This is text that the King's Altar of Earth has a god of grain.
translations.idiomatic: This is textual evidence that the King's Altar of Earth has a god of grain.

sentences.zh: 封人設壝之無稷字，說者以為略文，從可知也。

translations.literal: The Border Officer setting the platform lacking the character for god of grain— expositors hold this abbreviated text; from this it may be known.
translations.idiomatic: The Border Officer setting the platform lacking the character for god of grain—expositors hold this abbreviated text; from this it may be known.

sentences.zh: 謂宜仍舊立二社，而加立帝社之稷。

translations.literal: I hold that one should still establish two altars of Earth as before, and additionally establish the god of grain at the imperial altar of Earth.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that one should still establish two altars of Earth as before, and additionally establish the god of grain at the Imperial Altar of Earth.

sentences.zh: 」時成粲議稱：「景侯論太社不立京都，欲破鄭氏學。

translations.literal: " At that time Cheng Can deliberated: "Jinghou's discussion that the Grand Altar of Earth is not established in the capital— wishes to break Master Zheng's school.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Cheng Can deliberated: "Jinghou's discussion that the Grand Altar of Earth is not established in the capital—wishes to break Master Zheng's school.

sentences.zh: 」咸重表以為：「如粲之論，景侯之解文以此壞。

translations.literal: " Xian resubmitted the memorial: "Following Can's discussion— Jinghou's exegesis is destroyed on this point.
translations.idiomatic: Xian resubmitted the memorial: "Following Can's discussion—Jinghou's exegesis is destroyed on this point.

sentences.zh: 大雅云：『乃立冢土。

translations.literal: The Great Odes state: 'Then established the mound of earth.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Odes state: 'Then he established the mound of earth.

sentences.zh: 』毛公解曰：『冢土，太社也。

translations.literal: ' Mao's commentary says: 'Mound of earth— the Grand Altar of Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Mao's commentary says: 'Mound of earth—the Grand Altar of Earth.

sentences.zh: 』景侯解詩，即用此說。

translations.literal: Jinghou explaining the Odes uses this doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: In Jinghou's explanation of the Odes, he uses this doctrine.

sentences.zh: 禹貢『惟土五色』。

translations.literal: The Tribute of Yu: 'Only the five colors of earth.
translations.idiomatic: The Tribute of Yu states: 'Only the five colors of earth.

sentences.zh: 景侯解曰：『王者取五色土為太社，封四方諸侯。

translations.literal: Jinghou explains: 'The king takes five-colored earth for the Grand Altar of Earth and enfeoffs the feudal lords of the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: Jinghou explains: 'The king takes five-colored earth for the Grand Altar of Earth and enfeoffs the feudal lords of the four directions with it.

sentences.zh: 各割其方色土者覆四方也。

translations.literal: Each cuts earth of his direction's color to cover the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: Each cuts earth of his direction's color in order to cover the four directions.

sentences.zh: 』如此，太社復為立京都也。

translations.literal: ' Thus the Grand Altar of Earth is again established in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Grand Altar of Earth is again established in the capital.

sentences.zh: 不知此論從何出而與解乖。

translations.literal: I do not know whence this discussion arose yet it contradicts the explanation.
translations.idiomatic: I do not know whence this discussion arose, yet it contradicts the explanation.

sentences.zh: 上違經記明文，下壞景侯之解。

translations.literal: Above it violates explicit text in the classics; below it destroys Jinghou's explanation.
translations.idiomatic: Above it violates explicit text in the classics; below it undermines Jinghou's explanation.

sentences.zh: 臣雖頑蔽，少長學問，不能默已，謹復續上。

translations.literal: Your subject, though dull and obscured, having studied from youth, cannot remain silent— respectfully resubmitting.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject, though dull and obscured, having studied from youth, cannot remain silent—respectfully resubmitting.

sentences.zh: 」劉寔與咸議同。

translations.literal: Liu Shi agreed with Xian's deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shi concurred with Xian's deliberation.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「社實一神，而相襲二位，眾議不同，何必改作，其便仍舊，一如魏制。」

translations.literal: An edict stated: "The altar of Earth is truly one spirit, yet two positions are inherited in succession; the collective deliberations differ— why must it be changed? For convenience retain the former practice, exactly as Wei regulations."
translations.idiomatic: An edict stated: "The altar of Earth is truly one spirit, yet two positions are inherited in succession; the collective deliberations differ—why must it be changed? For convenience retain the former practice, exactly as Wei regulations."

sentences.zh: 至元帝建武元年，又依洛京立二社一稷。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianwu under Emperor Yuan, again following Luoyang established two altars of Earth and one god of grain.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianwu under Emperor Yuan, again following Luoyang, the court established two altars of Earth and one god of grain.

sentences.zh: 其太社之祝曰：「地德普施，惠存無疆。

translations.literal: The prayer of the Grand Altar of Earth states: "Earth's virtue universally spreads; favor preserved without limit.
translations.idiomatic: The prayer of the Grand Altar of Earth reads: "Earth's virtue universally spreads; favor preserved without limit.

sentences.zh: 乃建太社，保佑萬邦。

translations.literal: Thus establishing the Grand Altar of Earth, protecting and blessing the myriad states.
translations.idiomatic: Thus establishing the Grand Altar of Earth to protect and bless the myriad states.

sentences.zh: 悠悠四海，咸賴嘉祥。

translations.literal: The distant four seas all rely on auspicious blessing.
translations.idiomatic: The distant four seas all rely upon auspicious blessing.

sentences.zh: 」其帝社之祝曰：「坤德厚載，王畿是保。

translations.literal: " The prayer of the Imperial Altar of Earth states: "Earth's virtue thickly carries; the royal domain is preserved.
translations.idiomatic: The prayer of the Imperial Altar of Earth states: "Earth's virtue thickly carries; the royal domain is preserved.

sentences.zh: 乃建帝社，以神地道。

translations.literal: Thus establishing the Imperial Altar of Earth, to spiritualize the way of earth.
translations.idiomatic: Thus establishing the Imperial Altar of Earth to spiritualize the way of earth.

sentences.zh: 明祀惟辰，景福來造。

translations.literal: Bright sacrifice only at the proper season; great blessing comes to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Bright sacrifice only at the proper season; great blessing comes forth.

sentences.zh: 」禮，左宗廟，右社稷。

translations.literal: " The Rites: left the ancestral temple, right the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites: left the ancestral temple, right the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 歷代遵之，故洛京社稷在廟之右，而江左又然也。

translations.literal: Successive generations followed this— therefore Luoyang's altars of soil and grain were right of the temple; east of the Yangtze likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Successive generations followed this—therefore Luoyang's altars of soil and grain were right of the temple; east of the Yangtze likewise.

sentences.zh: 吳時宮東門雩門，疑吳社亦在宮東，與其廟同所也。

translations.literal: In Wu times the palace's east gate was the Rain Gate— I suspect Wu's altar of Earth was also east of the palace, in the same place as its temple.
translations.idiomatic: In Wu times the palace's east gate was the Rain Gate—I suspect Wu's altar of Earth was also east of the palace, in the same place as its temple.

sentences.zh: 宋仍舊，無所改作。

translations.literal: Song retained the former practice without change.
translations.idiomatic: Song retained the former practice without alteration.

sentences.zh: 魏氏三祖皆親耕籍，此則先農無廢享也。

translations.literal: Wei's three founding emperors all personally plowed the field of sacrifice— thus the Prior Farmer's sacrifice was not abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's three founding emperors all personally plowed the field of sacrifice—thus the Prior Farmer's sacrifice was not abandoned.

sentences.zh: 其禮無異聞，宜從漢儀。

translations.literal: The ritual differs without report— should follow Han practice.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual differs without report—should follow Han practice.

sentences.zh: 執事告祠以太牢。

translations.literal: The responsible official announces sacrifice with the Grand Victim.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible official announces the sacrifice with the Grand Victim.

sentences.zh: 晉元、哀帝並欲籍田而不遂，儀注亦闕略。

translations.literal: Emperors Yuan and Ai of Jin both wished to plow the field of sacrifice but did not succeed; the ritual instructions are also abbreviated.
translations.idiomatic: Emperors Yuan and Ai of Jin both wished to plow the field of sacrifice but did not succeed; the ritual instructions are also incomplete.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉二十一年春，親耕，乃立先農壇於籍田中阡西陌南。

translations.literal: In spring of the twenty-first year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen of Song, personal plowing— then established the Prior Farmer altar in the field of sacrifice west of the north-south path, south of the east-west path.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the twenty-first year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen of Song, personal plowing—then established the Prior Farmer altar in the field of sacrifice west of the north-south path, south of the east-west path.

sentences.zh: 高四尺，方二丈。

translations.literal: Four feet high; two zhang square.
translations.idiomatic: It was four feet high and two zhang square.

sentences.zh: 為四出陛。

translations.literal: Four ascending steps on four sides.
translations.idiomatic: There were four ascending steps on four sides.

sentences.zh: 陛廣五尺，外加埒。

translations.literal: Steps five feet wide; outside added an embankment.
translations.idiomatic: The steps were five feet wide; outside an embankment was added.

sentences.zh: 去阡陌各二十丈。

translations.literal: Twenty zhang from each field path.
translations.idiomatic: It stood twenty zhang from each field path.

sentences.zh: 車駕未到，司空、大司農率太祝令及眾執事質明以一太牢告祠。

translations.literal: Before the imperial carriage arrived, the Minister of Works and Grand Minister of Agriculture led the Director of Sacrifice and all responsible officials at dawn to announce sacrifice with one Grand Victim.
translations.idiomatic: Before the imperial carriage arrived, the Minister of Works and Grand Minister of Agriculture led the Director of Sacrifice and all responsible officials at dawn to announce the sacrifice with one Grand Victim.

sentences.zh: 祭器用祭社稷器。

translations.literal: Sacrificial vessels used the vessels for sacrificing at the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: The sacrificial vessels used were those for sacrificing at the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 祠畢，班餘胙於奉祠者。

translations.literal: When sacrifice was complete, distributed remaining sacrificial meat to those performing sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: When the sacrifice was complete, remaining sacrificial meat was distributed to those performing the rites.

sentences.zh: 舊典先農又常列於郊祭云。

translations.literal: Former canon also regularly listed the Prior Farmer at suburban sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Former canon also regularly listed the Prior Farmer among suburban sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 漢儀，皇后親桑東郊苑中。

translations.literal: Han practice: the empress personally tended mulberry trees in the eastern suburban park.
translations.idiomatic: Han practice held that the empress personally tended mulberry trees in the eastern suburban park.

sentences.zh: 蠶室祭蠶神曰：「苑窳婦人，寓氏公主。

translations.literal: The Silkworm Chamber sacrificed to the silkworm spirit— called: "Lady of the Park's Hollow, Princess of the Yu clan.
translations.idiomatic: The Silkworm Chamber sacrificed to the silkworm spirit—called: "Lady of the Park's Hollow, Princess of the Yu clan.

sentences.zh: 」祠用少牢。

translations.literal: " Sacrifice used the Lesser Victim.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice used the Lesser Victim.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太康九年，楊皇后躬桑于西郊，祀先蠶。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Taikang under Emperor Wu of Jin, Empress Yang personally tended mulberry at the western suburb and sacrificed to the Prior Silkworm.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Taikang under Emperor Wu of Jin, Empress Yang personally tended mulberry at the western suburb and sacrificed to the Prior Silkworm deity.

sentences.zh: 壇高一丈，方二丈，為四出陛，陛廣五尺。

translations.literal: Altar one zhang high, two zhang square, four ascending steps, steps five feet wide.
translations.idiomatic: The altar was one zhang high and two zhang square, with four ascending steps five feet wide.

sentences.zh: 在採桑壇東南帷宮之外，去帷宮十丈。

translations.literal: Outside the curtained palace southeast of the mulberry-gathering altar— ten zhang from the curtained palace.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the curtained palace southeast of the mulberry-gathering altar—ten zhang from the curtained palace.

sentences.zh: 皇后未到，太祝令質明以一太牢告祠。

translations.literal: Before the empress arrived, the Director of Sacrifice at dawn announced sacrifice with one Grand Victim.
translations.idiomatic: Before the empress arrived, the Director of Sacrifice at dawn announced the sacrifice with one Grand Victim.

sentences.zh: 謁者一人監祠。

translations.literal: One Attendant supervised sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: One Attendant supervised the sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 畢，徹饌，班餘胙於從桑及奉祠者。

translations.literal: When complete, removed the offerings; distributed remaining sacrificial meat to those tending mulberry and performing sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: When complete, the offerings were removed and remaining sacrificial meat distributed to those tending mulberry and performing the rites.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝黃初二年六月庚子，初禮五嶽四瀆，咸秩羣祀，瘞沈珪璋。

translations.literal: On the gengzi day of the sixth month of the second year of Huangchu under Emperor Wen of Wei, first performed ritual to the five sacred mountains and four great rivers; all ranked sacrifices were ordered; buried and submerged jade tablets.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengzi day of the sixth month in the second year of Huangchu under Emperor Wen of Wei, first performed ritual to the five sacred mountains and four great rivers; all ranked sacrifices were ordered; buried and submerged jade tablets.

sentences.zh: 六年七月，帝以舟軍入淮。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the sixth year the emperor entered the Huai by naval force.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the sixth year, the emperor entered the Huai River by naval force.

sentences.zh: 九月壬戌，遣使者沈璧于淮，禮也。

translations.literal: On the renxu day of the ninth month, dispatched envoys to submerge jade disks in the Huai— ritual practice.
translations.idiomatic: On the renxu day of the ninth month, dispatched envoys to submerge jade disks in the Huai—ritual practice.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝太和四年八月，帝東巡，遣使者以特牛祠中嶽，禮也。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fourth year of Taihe under Emperor Ming of Wei, the emperor toured east; dispatched envoys to sacrifice to the Central Sacred Mountain with a special ox— ritual practice.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the fourth year of Taihe under Emperor Ming of Wei, the emperor toured east; dispatched envoys to sacrifice to the Central Sacred Mountain with a special ox—ritual practice.

sentences.zh: 魏元帝咸熙元年，帝行幸長安，遣使者以璧幣禮華山，禮也。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianxi under Emperor Yuan of Wei, the emperor traveled to Chang'an; dispatched envoys to sacrifice to Mount Hua with jade disks and silk— ritual practice.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianxi under Emperor Yuan of Wei, the emperor traveled to Chang'an; dispatched envoys to sacrifice to Mount Hua with jade disks and silk—ritual practice.

sentences.zh: 晉穆帝升平中，何琦論修五嶽祠曰：「唐、虞之制，天子五載一巡狩，省時之方，柴燎五嶽，望于山川，徧于羣神。

translations.literal: In the Shengping era under Emperor Mu of Jin, He Qi deliberated on repairing sacrifice to the five sacred mountains: "The system of Tang and Yu— the Son of Heaven every five years made one inspection tour, examining the seasons of each region; burned firewood at the five sacred mountains; gazed toward mountains and rivers; extending to all spirits.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shengping era under Emperor Mu of Jin, He Qi deliberated on repairing sacrifice to the five sacred mountains: "The system of Tang and Yu—the Son of Heaven every five years made one inspection tour, examining the seasons of each region; burned firewood at the five sacred mountains; gazed toward mountains and rivers; extending to all spirits.

sentences.zh: 故曰『因名山升中于天』。

translations.literal: Therefore it says 'by famous mountains ascend to the center of heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the text says 'by famous mountains one ascends to the center of heaven.

sentences.zh: 所以昭告神祇，饗報功德。

translations.literal: This is to declare and inform the spirits; feast and recompense merit.
translations.idiomatic: This is to declare and inform the spirits, and to feast and recompense merit.

sentences.zh: 是以災厲不作，而風雨寒暑以時。

translations.literal: Therefore calamities and pestilence do not arise; wind, rain, cold, and heat come at their seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore calamities and pestilence do not arise, and wind, rain, cold, and heat come at their seasons.

sentences.zh: 降逮三代，年數雖殊，而其禮不易。

translations.literal: Descending to the three dynasties— though the number of years differed, the ritual did not change.
translations.idiomatic: Descending to the three dynasties—though the number of years differed, the ritual did not change.

sentences.zh: 五嶽視三公，四瀆視諸侯，著在經記，所謂有其舉之，莫敢廢也。

translations.literal: The five sacred mountains equal the three excellencies; the four great rivers equal feudal lords— recorded in the classics; what is called: when there is an occasion to perform it, none dare abandon it.
translations.idiomatic: The five sacred mountains equal the three excellencies; the four great rivers equal feudal lords—recorded in the classics; what is called: when there is an occasion to perform it, none dare abandon it.

sentences.zh: 及秦、漢都西京，涇、渭長水，雖不在祀典，以近咸陽，故盡得比大川之祠。

translations.literal: When Qin and Han established the capital in the west, the Jing and Wei long flowed— though not in the canon of sacrifice, being near Xianyang, all could be compared to sacrifice to great rivers.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin and Han established the capital in the west, the Jing and Wei long flowed—though not in the canon of sacrifice, being near Xianyang, all could be compared to sacrifice to great rivers.

sentences.zh: 而正立之祀，可以闕哉！

translations.literal: Yet the orthodox established sacrifice— can it be omitted!
translations.idiomatic: Yet the orthodox established sacrifice—can it be omitted!

sentences.zh: 自永嘉之亂，神州傾覆，茲事替矣。

translations.literal: Since the chaos of Yongjia the divine land was overturned— this affair was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Since the chaos of Yongjia the divine land was overturned—this affair was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 唯灊之天柱，在王略之內，舊臺選百石吏卒，以奉其職。

translations.literal: Only Qian's Heavenly Pillar, within the royal domain— formerly the old platform selected one hundred-shi officials and soldiers to fulfill the duty.
translations.idiomatic: Only Qian's Heavenly Pillar, within the royal domain—formerly the old platform selected one hundred-shi officials and soldiers to fulfill the duty.

sentences.zh: 中興之際，未有官守，廬江郡常遣大吏兼假，四時禱賽，春釋寒而冬請冰。

translations.literal: At the restoration there was no official custodian; Lujiang commandery regularly dispatched a senior official concurrently acting; four seasonal prayer and sacrifice; spring releasing cold, winter requesting ice.
translations.idiomatic: At the restoration there was no official custodian; Lujiang commandery regularly dispatched a senior official to serve concurrently; four seasonal prayers and sacrifices were held—spring releasing cold, winter requesting ice.

sentences.zh: 咸和迄今，已復墮替。

translations.literal: From Xianhe to the present, again fallen into disuse.
translations.idiomatic: From Xianhe to the present, the practice had again fallen into disuse.

sentences.zh: 計今非典之祠，可謂非一。

translations.literal: Calculating now— non-canonical sacrifices, one may say, are not one.
translations.idiomatic: Calculating now—non-canonical sacrifices, one may say, are not one.

sentences.zh: 考其正名，則淫昏之鬼；

translations.literal: Examining their orthodox names— they are spirits of excess and confusion;
translations.idiomatic: Examining their orthodox names—they are spirits of excess and confusion;

sentences.zh: 推其糜費，則四民之蠹。

translations.literal: extrapolating their wasteful expense— they are parasites of the four classes of people.
translations.idiomatic: extrapolating their wasteful expense—they are parasites of the four classes of people.

sentences.zh: 而山川大神，更為簡闕，禮俗頹紊，人神雜擾，公私奔蹙，漸以滋繁。

translations.literal: Yet the great spirits of mountains and rivers are further simplified and omitted; ritual and custom decline in disorder; human and spirit mixed in disturbance; public and private pressed in haste— gradually growing ever more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the great spirits of mountains and rivers are further simplified and omitted; ritual and custom decline in disorder; human and spirit mixed in disturbance; public and private pressed in haste—gradually growing ever more numerous.

sentences.zh: 良由頃國家多難，日不暇給，草建廢滯，事有未遑。

translations.literal: Truly because in recent times the state had many calamities and days allowed no surplus— hastily establishing what was abandoned and stagnant, affairs had no time for completion.
translations.idiomatic: Truly because in recent times the state had many calamities and days allowed no surplus—hastily establishing what was abandoned and stagnant, affairs had no time for completion.

sentences.zh: 今元憝已殲，宜修舊典。

translations.literal: Now the great villain is destroyed— the former canon should be repaired.
translations.idiomatic: Now the great villain is destroyed—the former canon should be repaired.

sentences.zh: 嶽瀆之域，風教所被，來蘇之人，咸蒙德澤，而神祇禋祀，未之或甄，巡狩柴燎，其廢尚矣。

translations.literal: The domain of mountains and rivers— where culture and teaching reach— people restored to life all receive virtuous favor; yet spirit sacrifice and reverent offering have not been distinguished; inspection tour and firewood burning— its abandonment is still great.
translations.idiomatic: The domain of mountains and rivers—where culture and teaching reach—people restored to life all receive virtuous favor; yet spirit sacrifice and reverent offering have not been distinguished; inspection tour and firewood burning—its abandonment is still great.

sentences.zh: 崇明前典，將俟皇輿北旋，稽古憲章，大釐制度。

translations.literal: Exalting and clarifying the prior canon— await the imperial carriage's northern return; examine antiquity's statutes; greatly rectify the system.
translations.idiomatic: Exalting and clarifying the prior canon—await the imperial carriage's northern return; examine antiquity's statutes; greatly rectify the system.

sentences.zh: 其五嶽、四瀆宜遵修之處，但俎豆牲牢，祝嘏文辭，舊章靡記。

translations.literal: The five sacred mountains and four great rivers— places that should follow repair— but sacrificial vessels and victims, prayer and blessing texts, old statutes have no record.
translations.idiomatic: The five sacred mountains and four great rivers—places that should follow repair—but sacrificial vessels and victims, prayer and blessing texts, old statutes have no record.

sentences.zh: 可令禮官作式，歸諸誠簡，以達明德馨香，如斯而已。

translations.literal: May order the ritual officers to compose forms; return to sincerity and simplicity— to express bright virtue's fragrance— no more than this.
translations.idiomatic: May order the ritual officers to compose forms; return to sincerity and simplicity—to express bright virtue's fragrance—no more than this.

sentences.zh: 其諸妖孽，可粗依法令，先去其甚。

translations.literal: As for various demonic aberrations— may roughly follow law and decree; first remove the most excessive.
translations.idiomatic: As for various demonic aberrations—may roughly follow law and decree; first remove the most excessive.

sentences.zh: 俾邪正不瀆。

translations.literal: Make the heterodox and orthodox not intermingle.
translations.idiomatic: Keep the heterodox and orthodox from intermingling.

sentences.zh: 」不見省。

translations.literal: " Not seen and approved.
translations.idiomatic: Not seen and approved.

sentences.zh: 宋孝武帝大明七年六月丙辰，有司奏：「詔奠祭霍山，未審應奉使何官？

translations.literal: On the bingchen day of the sixth month of the seventh year of Daming, the responsible officials memorialized: "An edict orders libation sacrifice at Mount Huo— it is unclear which official should be dispatched?
translations.idiomatic: On the bingchen day of the sixth month in the seventh year of Daming, the responsible officials memorialized: "An edict orders libation sacrifice at Mount Huo—it is unclear which official should be dispatched?

sentences.zh: 用何牲饌？

translations.literal: What victims and offerings should be used?
translations.idiomatic: What victims and offerings ought to be used?

sentences.zh: 進奠之日，又用何器？

translations.literal: On the day of advancing libation— what vessels should be used?
translations.idiomatic: On the day of advancing libation—what vessels should be used?

sentences.zh: 」殿中郎丘景先議：「修祀川嶽，道光列代；

translations.literal: " Palace Gentleman Qiu Jingxian argued: "Repairing sacrifice to rivers and mountains— the Way illumines successive generations;
translations.idiomatic: Palace Gentleman Qiu Jingxian argued: "Repairing sacrifice to rivers and mountains—the Way illumines successive generations;

sentences.zh: 差秩珪璋，義昭聯冊。

translations.literal: ranking jade tablets and scepters— meaning clarifies linked registers.
translations.idiomatic: ranking jade tablets and scepters—meaning clarifies linked registers.

sentences.zh: 但業曠中葉，儀漏典文。

translations.literal: Yet the enterprise was abandoned in the middle age; ritual leaked from canonical text.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the enterprise was abandoned in the middle age, and ritual leaked away from canonical text.

sentences.zh: 尋姬典事繼宗伯，漢載持節侍祠，血祭埋沈，經垂明範，酒脯牢具，悉有詳例。
