translations.literal: Examining Zhou canon— the affair continued with the Director of Ritual; Han records bear credentials and attend sacrifice; blood sacrifice, burial, and submersion— classics display bright models; wine, dried meat, and victims— all have detailed examples.
translations.idiomatic: Examining Zhou canon—the affair continued with the Director of Ritual; Han records bear credentials and attend sacrifice; blood sacrifice, burial, and submersion—classics display bright models; wine, dried meat, and victims—all have detailed examples.

sentences.zh: 又名山著珪幣之異，大冢有嘗禾之加。

translations.literal: Also famous mountains have the distinction of jade disks and silk; great mounds have the addition of tasting the grain.
translations.idiomatic: Also famous mountains have the distinction of jade disks and silk offerings; great mounds have the addition of tasting the grain.

sentences.zh: 山海祠霍山，以太牢告玉，此準酌記傳，其可言者也。

translations.literal: Classic of Mountains and Seas sacrifices to Mount Huo with Grand Victim announcing jade— this following and measuring records and transmissions may be spoken of.
translations.idiomatic: Classic of Mountains and Seas sacrifices to Mount Huo with Grand Victim announcing jade—this following and measuring records and transmissions may be spoken of.

sentences.zh: 今皇風緬暢，輝祀通嶽，愚謂宜使以太常持節，牲以太牢之具，羞用酒脯時穀，禮以赤璋纁幣。

translations.literal: Now imperial influence extends far; brilliant sacrifice reaches the peaks— I hold that the Director of Ceremonies should bear credentials; victims use Grand Victim provisions; offerings use wine, dried meat, and seasonal grain; ritual uses red jade tablet and crimson silk.
translations.idiomatic: Now imperial influence extends far; brilliant sacrifice reaches the peaks—I hold that the Director of Ceremonies should bear credentials; victims use Grand Victim provisions; offerings use wine, dried meat, and seasonal grain; ritual uses red jade tablet and crimson silk.

sentences.zh: 又鬯人之職，『凡山川四方用蜃』，則盛酒當以蠡杯，其餘器用，無所取說。

translations.literal: Also the office of the Fragrant Wine Maker: 'For mountains, rivers, and the four directions use oyster shells'— then wine vessels should use shell cups; other vessels— no source for explanation.
translations.idiomatic: Also the office of the Fragrant Wine Maker: 'For mountains, rivers, and the four directions use oyster shells'—then wine vessels should use shell cups; other vessels—no source for explanation.

sentences.zh: 按郊望山瀆，以質表誠，器尚陶匏，籍以茅席，近可依準。

translations.literal: Examining suburban gazing at mountains and rivers— with substance expressing sincerity; vessels prefer pottery and gourds; mats use rush— recent practice may be followed.
translations.idiomatic: Examining suburban gazing at mountains and rivers—with substance expressing sincerity; vessels prefer pottery and gourds; mats use rush—recent practice may be followed.

sentences.zh: 山川以兆，宜為壇域。

translations.literal: Mountains and rivers by divination— an altar domain should be made.
translations.idiomatic: Mountains and rivers by divination—an altar domain should be made.

sentences.zh: 」參議景先議為允。

translations.literal: " Upon joint deliberation Jingxian's view was held acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Upon joint deliberation Jingxian's view was held acceptable.

sentences.zh: 令以兼太常持節奉使，牲用太牢，加以璋幣，器用陶匏，時不復用蜃，宜同郊祀，以爵獻。

translations.literal: An order had the Concurrent Director of Ceremonies bear credentials as envoy; victims use Grand Victim; additionally jade tablet and silk; vessels use pottery and gourds; at the time oyster shells were no longer used— should follow suburban sacrifice and offer with wine cups.
translations.idiomatic: An order had the Concurrent Director of Ceremonies bear credentials as envoy; victims use Grand Victim; additionally jade tablet and silk; vessels use pottery and gourds; at the time oyster shells were no longer used—should follow suburban sacrifice and offer with wine cups.

sentences.zh: 凡肴饌種數，一依社祭為允。

translations.literal: All prepared dishes in number— follow altar of Earth sacrifice as acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: All prepared dishes in number—follow altar of Earth sacrifice as acceptable.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝咸寧二年春，久旱。

translations.literal: In spring of the second year of Xianning under Emperor Wu of Jin, long drought.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the second year of Xianning under Emperor Wu of Jin, drought persisted long.

sentences.zh: 四月丁巳，詔曰：「諸旱處廣加祈請。

translations.literal: On the dingsi day of the fourth month, an edict stated: "At all drought places broadly add prayer and petition.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingsi day of the fourth month, an edict stated: "At all drought-stricken places, broadly add prayer and petition.

sentences.zh: 」五月庚午，始祈雨于社稷山川。

translations.literal: On the gengwu day of the fifth month, first prayed for rain at the altars of soil and grain, mountains, and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengwu day of the fifth month, the court first prayed for rain at the altars of soil and grain, mountains, and rivers.

sentences.zh: 六月戊子，獲澍雨。

translations.literal: On the wuzi day of the sixth month, timely rain was obtained.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuzi day of the sixth month, timely rain fell.

sentences.zh: 此雩禜舊典也。

translations.literal: This is the old canon of yu and yong sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: This is the old canon of yu and yong rain sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 太康三年四月、十年二月，又如之。

translations.literal: The fourth month of the third year of Taikang and the second month of the tenth year— again as such.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth month of the third year of Taikang and the second month of the tenth year—again as such.

sentences.zh: 是後修之至今。

translations.literal: Thereafter it was maintained to the present.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the practice was maintained down to the present.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝黃初二年正月，詔曰：「昔仲尼資大聖之才，懷帝王之器，當衰周之末，無受命之運，乃退考五代之禮，修素王之事，因魯史而制春秋，就太師而正雅、頌，俾千載之後，莫不宗其文以述作，仰其聖以成謀。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Huangchu under Emperor Wen of Wei, an edict stated: "Formerly Zhongni possessed the talent of the greatest sage, harbored the vessel of emperors and kings; at the end of declining Zhou he had no mandate of fortune— then retired to examine the ritual of five dynasties, cultivated the affairs of the uncrowned king; based on Lu chronicles to compose the Spring and Autumn Annals; approached the Grand Master to rectify the Ya and Song; causing after a thousand years none not to take his texts as model for composition, look up to his sagehood to complete plans.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year of Huangchu under Emperor Wen of Wei, an edict stated: "Formerly Zhongni possessed the talent of the greatest sage, harbored the vessel of emperors and kings; at the end of declining Zhou he had no mandate of fortune—then retired to examine the ritual of five dynasties, cultivated the affairs of the uncrowned king; based on Lu chronicles to compose the Spring and Autumn Annals; approached the Grand Master to rectify the Ya and Song; causing after a thousand years none not to take his texts as model for composition, look up to his sagehood to complete plans.

sentences.zh: 茲可謂命世大聖，億載之師表者也。

translations.literal: This may be called a sage of the age, a teacher for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: This may be called a sage of the age and a teacher for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 以遭天下大亂，百祀隳廢，舊居之廟，毀而不修，褒成之後，絕而莫繼，闕里不聞講頌之聲，四時不覩烝嘗之位，斯豈所謂崇化報功，盛德百世必祀者哉！

translations.literal: Because the realm fell into great chaos, the hundred sacrifices were destroyed and abandoned; the temple of his old residence ruined and not repaired; the Marquis who received enfeoffment cut off with none to continue; in Que village no sound of lecture and recitation; in the four seasons no sight of zheng and chang positions— is this what is called exalting transformation and recompensing merit, flourishing virtue that a hundred generations must sacrifice to?
translations.idiomatic: Because the realm fell into great chaos, the hundred sacrifices were destroyed and abandoned; the temple of his old residence ruined and not repaired; the Marquis who received enfeoffment cut off with none to continue; in Que village no sound of lecture and recitation; in the four seasons no sight of zheng and chang positions—is this what is called exalting transformation and recompensing merit, flourishing virtue that a hundred generations must sacrifice to?

sentences.zh: 其以議郎孔羨為宗聖侯，邑百戶，奉孔子祀。

translations.literal: Appoint Discussion Gentleman Kong Xian as Marquis of the Ancestral Sage, fief of one hundred households, to perform sacrifice to Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: Discussion Gentleman Kong Xian was appointed Marquis of the Ancestral Sage, with a fief of one hundred households, to perform sacrifice to Confucius.

sentences.zh: 命魯郡修舊廟，置百戶吏卒，以守衞之。」

translations.literal: Order Lu commandery to repair the old temple; establish one hundred households of officials and soldiers to guard it."
translations.idiomatic: Lu commandery was ordered to repair the old temple and to establish one hundred households of officials and soldiers to guard it."

sentences.zh: 晉武帝泰始三年十一月，改封宗聖侯孔震為奉聖亭侯。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the third year of Taishi under Emperor Wu of Jin, changed the enfeoffment of Marquis of the Ancestral Sage Kong Zhen to Marquis of Fengsheng District.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the third year of Taishi under Emperor Wu of Jin, the enfeoffment of Marquis of the Ancestral Sage Kong Zhen was changed to Marquis of Fengsheng District.

sentences.zh: 又詔太學及魯國四時備三牲以祀孔子。

translations.literal: Also an edict: the Imperial Academy and Lu state in the four seasons prepare three victims to sacrifice to Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also ordered the Imperial Academy and the state of Lu to prepare three victims in the four seasons to sacrifice to Confucius.

sentences.zh: 明帝太寧三年，詔給事奉聖亭侯孔亭四時祠孔子，祭宜如泰始故事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taining under Emperor Ming, an edict: Attendant-in-Service Marquis of Fengsheng District Kong Ting— four seasonal sacrifices to Confucius; sacrifice should follow the Taishi precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taining under Emperor Ming, an edict: Attendant-in-Service Marquis of Fengsheng District Kong Ting—four seasonal sacrifices to Confucius; sacrifice should follow the Taishi precedent.

sentences.zh: 亭五代孫繼之博塞無度，常以祭直顧進，替慢不祀。

translations.literal: Ting's fifth-generation descendant Jizhi gambled without limit; often used sacrificial funds for advance payment— negligent and disrespectful, not sacrificing.
translations.idiomatic: Ting's fifth-generation descendant Jizhi gambled without limit; often used sacrificial funds for advance payment—negligent and disrespectful, not sacrificing.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉八年，有司奏奪爵。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen of Song, the responsible officials memorialized to strip the title.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen of Song, the responsible officials memorialized to strip the marquisate.

sentences.zh: 至十九年，又授孔隱之。

translations.literal: By the nineteenth year, again enfeoffed Kong Yinzhi.
translations.idiomatic: By the nineteenth year, Kong Yinzhi was again enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 兄子熙先謀逆，又失爵。

translations.literal: His elder brother's son Xixian plotted rebellion— again lost the title.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother's son Xixian plotted rebellion—again lost the title.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，更以孔惠雲為奉聖侯。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, again made Kong Huiyun Marquis of Fengsheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year, Kong Huiyun was again made Marquis of Fengsheng.

sentences.zh: 後有重疾，失爵。

translations.literal: Later had serious illness— lost the title.
translations.idiomatic: Later had serious illness—lost the title.

sentences.zh: 孝武大明二年，又以孔邁為奉聖侯。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daming under Emperor Xiaowu, again made Kong Mai Marquis of Fengsheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Daming under Emperor Xiaowu, Kong Mai was again made Marquis of Fengsheng.

sentences.zh: 邁卒，子荂嗣，有罪，失爵。

translations.literal: Mai died; son Cha succeeded; had offense— lost the title.
translations.idiomatic: Mai died; son Cha succeeded; had offense—lost the title.

sentences.zh: 魏齊王正始二年三月，帝講論語通，五年五月，講尚書通，七年十二月，講禮記通，並使太常釋奠，以太牢祀孔子於辟雍，以顏淵配。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year of Zhengshi under Emperor Qi of Wei, the emperor completed lecture on the Analects; fifth month fifth year completed lecture on the Documents; twelfth month seventh year completed lecture on the Record of Rites— all ordered the Director of Ceremonies to perform libation sacrifice; sacrificed to Confucius at the Bright Hall with Grand Victim; Yan Yuan as associate.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second year of Zhengshi under Emperor Qi of Wei, the emperor completed lecture on the Analects; fifth month fifth year completed lecture on the Documents; twelfth month seventh year completed lecture on the Record of Rites—all ordered the Director of Ceremonies to perform libation sacrifice; sacrificed to Confucius at the Bright Hall with Grand Victim; Yan Yuan as associate.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝泰始七年，皇太子講孝經通，咸寧三年，講詩通，太康三年，〔講禮記通，惠帝元康三年，皇太子〕講論語通，元帝太興三年，皇太子講論語通，太子並親釋奠，以太牢祠孔子，以顏淵配。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taishi under Emperor Wu of Jin, the Heir Apparent completed lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety; third year of Xianning completed lecture on the Odes; third year of Taikang [completed lecture on the Record of Rites; third year of Yuan Kang under Emperor Hui, the Heir Apparent] completed lecture on the Analects; third year of Taixing under Emperor Yuan, the Heir Apparent completed lecture on the Analects— the Heir Apparent all personally performed libation sacrifice; sacrificed to Confucius with Grand Victim; Yan Yuan as associate.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Taishi under Emperor Wu of Jin, the Heir Apparent completed lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety; third year of Xianning completed lecture on the Odes; third year of Taikang [completed lecture on the Record of Rites; third year of Yuan Kang under Emperor Hui, the Heir Apparent] completed lecture on the Analects; third year of Taixing under Emperor Yuan, the Heir Apparent completed lecture on the Analects—the Heir Apparent all personally performed libation sacrifice; sacrificed to Confucius with Grand Victim; Yan Yuan as associate.

sentences.zh: 成帝咸康元年，帝講詩通，穆帝升平元年三月，帝講孝經通，孝武寧康三年七月，帝講孝經通，並釋奠如故事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiankang under Emperor Cheng, the emperor completed lecture on the Odes; third month first year of Shengping under Emperor Mu, the emperor completed lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety; seventh month third year of Ningkang under Emperor Xiaowu, the emperor completed lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety— all performed libation sacrifice as in former precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xiankang under Emperor Cheng, the emperor completed lecture on the Odes; third month first year of Shengping under Emperor Mu, the emperor completed lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety; seventh month third year of Ningkang under Emperor Xiaowu, the emperor completed lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety—all performed libation sacrifice as in former precedent.

sentences.zh: 穆帝、孝武並權以中堂為太學。

translations.literal: Emperors Mu and Xiaowu both provisionally used the central hall as the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Emperors Mu and Xiaowu both provisionally used the central hall for the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉二十二年四月，皇太子講孝經通，釋奠國子學，如晉故事。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the twenty-second year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen of Song, the Heir Apparent completed lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety; performed libation sacrifice at the National University— as Jin precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the twenty-second year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen of Song, the Heir Apparent completed lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety; performed libation sacrifice at the National University—as Jin precedent.

sentences.zh: 漢東海恭王薨，明帝出幸津門亭發哀。

translations.literal: When Prince Gong of Donghai in Han died, Emperor Ming went out to Jinmen Pavilion to express mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Gong of Donghai died in Han, Emperor Ming went out to Jinmen Pavilion to express mourning.

sentences.zh: 魏時會喪及使者弔祭，用博士杜希議，皆去玄冠，加以布巾。

translations.literal: In Wei times at assembly mourning and when envoys performed condolence sacrifice— following Erudite Du Xi's deliberation— all removed the black cap and added cloth headcloth.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei times at assembly mourning and when envoys performed condolence sacrifice—following Erudite Du Xi's deliberation—all removed the black cap and added cloth headcloth.

sentences.zh: 魏武帝少時，漢太尉橋玄獨先禮異焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Wei was young, Han Grand Commandant Qiao Xuan alone first treated him with special ritual distinction.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Wei was young, Han Grand Commandant Qiao Xuan alone first treated him with special ritual honor.

sentences.zh: 故建安中，遣使祠以太牢。

translations.literal: Therefore in the Jianan era dispatched envoys to sacrifice with Grand Victim.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore in the Jianan era he dispatched envoys to sacrifice with the Grand Victim.

sentences.zh: 文帝黃初六年十二月，過梁郡，又以太牢祠之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the sixth year of Huangchu under Emperor Wen, passing through Liang commandery, again sacrificed with Grand Victim.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the sixth year of Huangchu under Emperor Wen, while passing through Liang commandery, he again sacrificed with the Grand Victim.

sentences.zh: 黃初二年正月，帝校獵至原陵，遣使者以太牢祠漢世祖。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Huangchu, the emperor reviewed the hunt at Yuanling; dispatched envoys to sacrifice to Han Emperor Guangwu with Grand Victim.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year of Huangchu, the emperor reviewed the hunt at Yuanling and dispatched envoys to sacrifice to Han Emperor Guangwu with the Grand Victim.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉二十五年四月丙辰，車駕行幸江寧，經司徒劉穆之墓，遣使致祭焉。

translations.literal: On the bingchen day of the fourth month of the twenty-fifth year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen of Song, the imperial carriage traveled to Jiangning; passing the tomb of Director of the Masters of Ceremony Liu Muzhi; dispatched envoys to perform sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingchen day of the fourth month in the twenty-fifth year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen of Song, the imperial carriage traveled to Jiangning; passing the tomb of Director of the Masters of Ceremony Liu Muzhi; dispatched envoys to perform sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝大明三年二月戊申，行幸籍田，經左光祿大夫袁湛墓，遣使致祭。

translations.literal: On the wushen day of the second month of the third year of Daming under Emperor Xiaowu, traveling to the field of sacrifice; passing the tomb of Left Grand Master of the Bright Hall Yuan Zhan; dispatched envoys to perform sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: On the wushen day of the second month in the third year of Daming under Emperor Xiaowu, traveling to the field of sacrifice; passing the tomb of Left Grand Master of the Bright Hall Yuan Zhan; dispatched envoys to perform sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 大明五年九月庚午，車駕行幸，經司空殷景仁墓，遣使致祭。

translations.literal: On the gengwu day of the ninth month of the fifth year of Daming, the imperial carriage traveled; passing the tomb of Minister of Works Yin Jingren; dispatched envoys to perform sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengwu day of the ninth month in the fifth year of Daming, the imperial carriage traveled; passing the tomb of Minister of Works Yin Jingren; dispatched envoys to perform sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 大明七年十一月，南巡。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the seventh year of Daming, toured south.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the seventh year of Daming, the emperor toured south.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，遣使祭晉大司馬桓溫、征西將軍毛璩墓。

translations.literal: On the yiyou day, dispatched envoys to sacrifice at the tombs of Jin Grand Commander Huan Wen and General Who Conquers the West Mao Jin.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiyou day, envoys were dispatched to sacrifice at the tombs of Jin Grand Commander Huan Wen and General Who Conquers the West Mao Jin.

sentences.zh: 劉禪景耀六年，詔為丞相諸葛亮立廟於沔陽。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jingyao under Liu Shan, an edict established a temple for Chancellor Zhuge Liang at Mianyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Jingyao under Liu Shan, an edict ordered a temple established for Chancellor Zhuge Liang at Mianyang.

sentences.zh: 先是所居各請立廟，不許，百姓遂私祭之。

translations.literal: Previously at each place he resided they requested to establish temples— not permitted; the people then privately sacrificed.
translations.idiomatic: Previously at each place he resided they requested to establish temples—not permitted; the people then privately sacrificed.

sentences.zh: 而言事者或以為可立於京師，乃從人意，皆不納。

translations.literal: Yet memorialists sometimes held that establishment in the capital was possible— following popular sentiment; none was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Yet memorialists sometimes held that establishment in the capital was possible—following popular sentiment; none was accepted.

sentences.zh: 步兵校尉習隆、中書侍郎向充等言於禪曰：「昔周人懷邵伯之美，甘棠為之不伐；

translations.literal: Infantry Commandant Xi Long and Palace Secretariat Gentleman Xiang Chong and others spoke to Shan: "Formerly the Zhou people cherished Duke of Shao's beauty— the sweet pear tree was therefore not cut down;
translations.idiomatic: Infantry Commandant Xi Long and Palace Secretariat Gentleman Xiang Chong and others spoke to Shan: "Formerly the Zhou people cherished Duke of Shao's beauty—the sweet pear tree was therefore not cut down;

sentences.zh: 越王思范蠡之功，鑄金以存其象。

translations.literal: the King of Yue remembered Fan Li's merit— cast gold to preserve his image.
translations.idiomatic: the King of Yue remembered Fan Li's merit—cast gold to preserve his image.

sentences.zh: 自漢興已來，小善小德，而圖形立廟者多矣；

translations.literal: Since Han arose, small goodness and small virtue— yet those whose images were drawn and temples established are many;
translations.idiomatic: Since Han arose, small goodness and small virtue—yet those whose images were drawn and temples established are many;

sentences.zh: 況亮德範遐邇，勳蓋季世，興王室之不壞，實斯人是賴。

translations.literal: how much more Liang— virtue and model reaching far; merit covering the age; preserving the royal house from destruction— truly this person was relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: how much more Liang—virtue and model reaching far; merit covering the age; preserving the royal house from destruction—truly this person was relied upon.

sentences.zh: 而烝嘗止於私門，廟象闕而莫立，百姓巷祭，戎夷野祀，非所以存德念功，述追在昔也。

translations.literal: Yet zheng and chang stopped at private gates; temple images lacking and not established; the hundred surnames sacrificed in lanes; barbarian warriors sacrificed in the wild— not the way to preserve virtue and recall merit, continuing to pursue the past.
translations.idiomatic: Yet zheng and chang stopped at private gates; temple images lacking and not established; the hundred surnames sacrificed in lanes; barbarian warriors sacrificed in the wild—not the way to preserve virtue and recall merit, continuing to pursue the past.

sentences.zh: 今若盡從人心，則瀆而無典；

translations.literal: Now if fully following popular sentiment— then excessive and without canon;
translations.idiomatic: Now if fully following popular sentiment—then excessive and without canon;

sentences.zh: 建之京師，又逼宗廟。

translations.literal: establishing in the capital again encroaches on the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Establishing it in the capital again encroaches upon the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 此聖懷所以惟疑也。

translations.literal: This is why the sage heart hesitates.
translations.idiomatic: This is why the sage's heart hesitates.

sentences.zh: 愚以為宜因近其墓，立之於沔陽，使屬所以時賜祭。

translations.literal: I hold that near his tomb it should be established at Mianyang; have the responsible office grant seasonal sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that it should be established near his tomb at Mianyang, and that the responsible office should grant seasonal sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 凡其故臣欲奉祠者，皆限至廟。

translations.literal: All former ministers wishing to perform sacrifice— all limited to the temple.
translations.idiomatic: All former ministers wishing to perform sacrifice—all limited to the temple.

sentences.zh: 斷其私祀，以崇正禮。

translations.literal: Cut off private sacrifice— to exalt orthodox ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Cut off private sacrifice—to exalt orthodox ritual.

sentences.zh: 」於是從之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon this was followed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon this was followed.

sentences.zh: 何承天曰：「周禮：『凡有功者祭於大烝。

translations.literal: He Chengtian said: "The Rites of Zhou: 'All who have merit sacrifice at the great zheng.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian said: "The Rites of Zhou state: 'All who have merit are sacrificed to at the great zheng.

sentences.zh: 』故後代遵之，以元勳配饗。

translations.literal: ' Therefore later generations followed this— meritorious ministers received paired feasting.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore later generations followed this—meritorious ministers received paired feasting.

sentences.zh: 充等曾不是式，禪又從之，並非禮也。」

translations.literal: Chong and others did not take this as model; Shan again followed them— both not ritual."
translations.idiomatic: Chong and others did not take this as model; Shan again followed them—both not ritual."

sentences.zh: 漢時城陽國人以劉章有功於漢，為之立祠。

translations.literal: In Han times the people of Chengyang state, because Liu Zhang had merit toward Han, established a temple for him.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times the people of Chengyang state, because Liu Zhang had rendered merit to Han, established a temple for him.

sentences.zh: 青州諸郡，轉相放效，濟南尤盛。

translations.literal: The commanderies of Qing province mutually imitated this; Jinan was especially flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: The commanderies of Qing province mutually imitated the practice; Jinan was especially flourishing.

sentences.zh: 至魏武帝為濟南相，皆毀絕之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Wei was magistrate of Jinan, all were destroyed and cut off.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Wei served as magistrate of Jinan, all such temples were destroyed and cut off.

sentences.zh: 及秉大政，普加除翦，世之淫祀遂絕。

translations.literal: When he held great governance, universally added removal and cutting— the age's excessive sacrifices were thereby ended.
translations.idiomatic: When he held great governance, universally added removal and cutting—the age's excessive sacrifices were thereby ended.

sentences.zh: 至文帝黃初五年十一月，詔曰：「先王制禮，所以昭孝事祖，大則郊社，其次宗廟，三辰五行，名山川澤，非此族也，不在祀典。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fifth year of Huangchu under Emperor Wen, an edict stated: "Former kings established ritual to clarify filial service to ancestors; great affairs are suburban altars and temples; the three luminaries and five phases, famous mountains and rivers— what is not of this category is not in the canon of sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the fifth year of Huangchu under Emperor Wen, an edict stated: "Former kings established ritual to clarify filial service to ancestors; great affairs are suburban altars and temples; the three luminaries and five phases, famous mountains and rivers—what is not of this category is not in the canon of sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 叔世衰亂，崇信巫史，至乃宮殿之內，戶牖之間，無不沃酹，甚矣其惑也。

translations.literal: Later ages declined in disorder; excessively trusted shamans and clerks— even within palace halls, between doors and windows, none without libation— how excessive the delusion!
translations.idiomatic: Later ages declined in disorder; excessively trusted shamans and clerks—even within palace halls, between doors and windows, none without libation—how excessive the delusion!

sentences.zh: 自今其敢設非禮之祭，巫祝之言，皆以執左道論，著于令。

translations.literal: From now whoever dares establish non-ritual sacrifice or shaman and clerk speech— all judged by practicing the left path; recorded in decree.
translations.idiomatic: From now whoever dares establish non-ritual sacrifice or shaman and clerk speech—all judged by practicing the left path; recorded in decree.

sentences.zh: 」明帝青龍元年，又詔：「郡國山川不在祀典者，勿祠。」

translations.literal: " In the first year of Qinglong under Emperor Ming, again an edict: "Commandery and state mountains and rivers not in the canon of sacrifice— do not sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qinglong under Emperor Ming, again an edict: "Commandery and state mountains and rivers not in the canon of sacrifice—do not sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 晉武帝泰始元年十二月，詔：「昔聖帝明王，修五嶽、四瀆，名山川澤，各有定制。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Taishi under Emperor Wu of Jin, an edict: "Formerly sage emperors and bright kings repaired the five sacred mountains, four great rivers, famous mountains and rivers— each had fixed regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the first year of Taishi under Emperor Wu of Jin, an edict: "Formerly sage emperors and bright kings repaired the five sacred mountains, four great rivers, famous mountains and rivers—each had fixed regulations.

sentences.zh: 所以報陰陽之功，而當幽明之道故也。

translations.literal: This is to recompense yin and yang's merit and accord with the way of the hidden and manifest.
translations.idiomatic: This is to recompense the merit of yin and yang and accord with the way of the hidden and manifest.

sentences.zh: 然以道莅天下者，其鬼不神，其神不傷人也。

translations.literal: Yet one who by the Way oversees the realm— his ghosts are not spirits; his spirits do not harm people.
translations.idiomatic: Yet one who by the Way oversees the realm—his ghosts are not spirits; his spirits do not harm people.

sentences.zh: 故祝史薦而無媿詞，是以其人敬慎幽冥，而淫祀不作。

translations.literal: Therefore the prayer clerk recommends without shameful words— thus those people reverently cautious toward the hidden; excessive sacrifice is not performed.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the prayer clerk recommends without shameful words—thus those people reverently cautious toward the hidden; excessive sacrifice is not performed.

sentences.zh: 末代信道不篤，僭禮瀆神，縱欲祈請，曾不敬而遠之，徒偷以求幸，妖妄相扇，舍正為邪，故魏朝疾之。

translations.literal: The final age's faith in the Way was not solid; excessive ritual profaned spirits; indulged desire in prayer and petition— never reverent yet distant; vainly stealing to seek fortune; demonic falsehood mutually incited; abandoning orthodox for heterodox— therefore Wei dynasty detested this.
translations.idiomatic: The final age's faith in the Way was not solid; excessive ritual profaned spirits; indulged desire in prayer and petition—never reverent yet distant; vainly stealing to seek fortune; demonic falsehood mutually incited; abandoning orthodox for heterodox—therefore Wei dynasty detested this.

sentences.zh: 其按舊禮，具為之制，使功著於人者，必有其報，而妖淫之鬼，不亂其間。

translations.literal: Examine the old ritual; fully make its regulations— let those whose merit is clear among people surely have recompense; and demonic excessive ghosts not disturb among them.
translations.idiomatic: Examine the old ritual; fully make its regulations—let those whose merit is clear among people surely have recompense; and demonic excessive ghosts not disturb among them.

sentences.zh: 」二年正月，有司奏：「春分祠厲殃及禳祠。

translations.literal: " In the first month of the second year, the responsible officials memorialized: "At the spring equinox sacrifice to pestilence spirits and exorcism sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year, the responsible officials memorialized: "At the spring equinox sacrifice to pestilence spirits and exorcism sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「不在祀典，除之。」

translations.literal: " An edict stated: "Not in the canon of sacrifice— remove them."
translations.idiomatic: An edict stated: "Not in the canon of sacrifice—remove them."

sentences.zh: 宋武帝永初二年，普禁淫祀。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongchu under Emperor Wu of Song, universally prohibited excessive sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongchu under Emperor Wu of Song, excessive sacrifice was universally prohibited.

sentences.zh: 由是蔣子文祠以下，普皆毀絕。

translations.literal: Thereupon from the temple of Jiang Ziwen downward— universally all destroyed and cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon from the temple of Jiang Ziwen downward—universally all destroyed and cut off.

sentences.zh: 孝武孝建初，更修起蔣山祠，所在山川，漸皆修復。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaojian under Emperor Xiaowu, again repaired and restored the Jiang Mountain temple; mountains and rivers everywhere gradually all repaired and restored.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xiaojian under Emperor Xiaowu, the Jiang Mountain temple was again repaired and restored; mountains and rivers everywhere were gradually repaired and restored as well.

sentences.zh: 明帝立九州廟於雞籠山，大聚羣神。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming established the Nine Provinces Temple at Jilong Mountain; greatly gathered all spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming established the Nine Provinces Temple at Jilong Mountain and greatly gathered all spirits there.

sentences.zh: 蔣侯宋代稍加爵，位至相國、大都督、中外諸軍事，加殊禮，鍾山王。

translations.literal: Marquis Jiang in Song times gradually received added rank— position reached Chancellor, Grand Commander, Commander of All Military Affairs Within and Without, with special ritual— Prince of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Jiang in Song times gradually received added rank—position reached Chancellor, Grand Commander, Commander of All Military Affairs Within and Without, with special ritual—Prince of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 蘇侯驃騎大將軍。

translations.literal: Marquis Su— General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Su—General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 四方諸神，咸加爵秩。

translations.literal: Spirits of the four directions all received added rank.
translations.idiomatic: Spirits of the four directions all received added titles and rank.

sentences.zh: 漢安帝元初四年，詔曰：「月令，『仲秋，養衰老，授几杖，行糜鬻』。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanchu under Emperor An of Han, an edict stated: "The Monthly Ordinance: 'Mid-autumn— nourish the aged and declining; grant staffs and stools; distribute congee and gruel.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yuanchu under Emperor An of Han, an edict stated: "The Monthly Ordinance: 'Mid-autumn—nourish the aged and declining; grant staffs and stools; distribute congee and gruel.

sentences.zh: 方今八月案比之時，郡縣多不奉行。

translations.literal: Now in the eighth month at the time of household registration— commanderies and counties mostly do not implement.
translations.idiomatic: Now in the eighth month at the time of household registration—commanderies and counties mostly do not implement.

sentences.zh: 雖有糜鬻，穅秕泥土相和半，不可飲食。

translations.literal: Although there is congee and gruel— chaff and dirt are mixed in half; not fit to drink or eat.
translations.idiomatic: Although there is congee and gruel—chaff and dirt are mixed in half; not fit to drink or eat.

sentences.zh: 」按此詔，漢時猶依月令施政事也。

translations.literal: " Examining this edict— Han times still followed the Monthly Ordinance in administering government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Examining this edict—Han times still followed the Monthly Ordinance in administering government affairs.
